弘治十五年進士登科錄

玉音

弘治十五年三月初八日，禮部尚書臣張昇等於奉天門奏：「為科舉事，會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少傅兼太子太傅、戶部尚書、謹身殿大學士劉健等五十六員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太傅、戶部尚書、謹身殿大學士劉健，庚辰進士。

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太傅、吏部尚書馬文升，辛未進士。

榮祿大夫、太子太保、刑部尚書閔珪，甲申進士。

資政大夫、太子少保、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士李東陽，甲申進士。
translation_en:
Register of Metropolitan Graduates for the Fifteenth Year of Hongzhi (1502)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the eighth day of the third month of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, your servant Zhang Sheng, Minister of Rites, and others memorialized at Fengtian Gate: “Concerning the civil-service examinations: in the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from throughout the empire, three hundred candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month this year, we request the appointment of fifty-six officials as examination readers and other officiating personnel, including Liu Jian, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct. The distinctions in status granted to the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class shall, as customary, comprise three men. The first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with all three granted the distinction ‘Presented Scholar with Honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the distinction ‘Presented Scholar.’ Those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the distinction ‘Associate Presented Scholar.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully recorded.

Examination Readers

Liu Jian, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct, was a metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year.

Ma Wensheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year.

Min Gui, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year.

Li Dongyang, Grand Master of Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Profundity, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi (1502), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in court robes, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the successful candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results placard out through Chang’an Left Gate, led by drums and music. After the placard had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-ranked graduate back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
… An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate was bestowed court robes, a cap, and a belt, and the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were bestowed paper currency.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a request to the throne, and the Ministry of Works was ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Kang Hai was registered in the civilian household category in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Dehan and was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Jue was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing; his grandfather Jian was Registrar in the Office of Transmission; and his father Yong was a prefectural Registrar. His mother was née Zhang. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Fu, Huai, Huan, and Ze, the last a Medical Instructor; his younger brothers were Run, Fu, Han, Chun, Yang, and Ying. He married a woman née Shang. He placed seventieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Qing was registered with Wuqing Guard in the Metropolitan Region and came from Yuyao County, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zhiqing and was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Bing, his grandfather Hong, and his father Bin, a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard. His mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cheng, and his younger brothers were Kan and Xun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingxiang was registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and came from Pu Subprefecture, Shandong. An additional student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Mengbi and was first in birth order, aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather Xian was an honorary official, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father Zan was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His mother, née Zhao, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Si and subsequently a woman née Xia. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second class: ninety-five men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Hu Yu 胡煜, courtesy name Tinghe, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Boliang; his grandfather, Minzhong; his father, Shi’ang; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Di, Qian, and Yao; his younger brothers were Yan and Can. He married a woman née Fang. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Duo 魯鐸, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jingling County, Mianyang Subprefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Zuyuan; his father, Shixian; and his mother, née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Zhen and Quan. He married a woman née Xiang. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Jin 薛金, courtesy name Zichun, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Peng; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Yun, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his mother, née Chen; and his stepmother, née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yong, authorized under the applicable regulations to wear official cap and sash; Xiang, a county clerk; Bin; Tang; and Chang. His younger brothers were Ao, Hua, and Rui. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Qian 蘇乾, courtesy name Tijian, was registered in a civilian household in Longqing Subprefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Changping County, Shuntian Prefecture. A subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Rong, was a Registrar; his father was Ming, whose annotation reads 坋 [?]. His mother was née Ding, and his stepmother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Han, Zhen, Ji, and Xuan. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Li. He ranked forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhang 李璋, courtesy name Defang, was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Jingning County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather, Xin, was posthumously granted the titles of Commandant of Manifest Trustworthiness and Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his father, Gui, was granted the same titles. His father's former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Repose; his mother, née Yan, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhen, an honorary official and Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; Cong, Grand Master for Comprehensive Service and Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and Rui, who was entitled to official cap and girdle by a provision of imperial grace. He married a woman née Qi and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shangjiong 王尚絅, courtesy name Jinfu, was registered in a military household in Jia County, Ruzhou, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Zong; his father, Xuan, an honorary official; and his mother, née Nie. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shangzhong, an honorary official, and Shangzhi; his younger brothers were Shangming and Shangjian. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jie 楊節, courtesy name Benzhong, was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Hefei County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Shun, was posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Might; his father, Sheng, was an Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His legal mother was née Ma, and his birth mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Qian, was an Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. He married a woman née Zhuang. He ranked 127th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Kun, registered in an official household of the Disciplinary Office of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a native of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Laifeng and ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Anshan; his grandfather, Zheng, was a company commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; and his father, Hong, was a surveillance vice commissioner. His mother, née He, was granted the title Lady for Service. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Qi was a jinshi of the same examination cohort; his younger brothers were Xiu, a battalion military judge in the Embroidered-uniform Guard, and Min. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Kui was registered in a civilian household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Tingyuan and ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ruiqu; his grandfather, Jingzhou; his father, Lizhong; and his mother, née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ding and Zhe. He married a woman née Zhang and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Wang. He ranked fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Renhe was registered in a civilian household in Huayang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Minhuai and ranked fourth among his brothers. He was twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Liangyi. His grandfather, Yanzhong, was a physician, received the honorary title Investigating Censor, and was posthumously granted the title Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father, Xi, was a left administration assistant commissioner. His mother, née Luo, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Repose; his stepmother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brothers were Shihe, Director of Music in an Office of Sacrificial Worship, Jinghe, and Yanghe; his younger brothers were Tianhe, Yonghe, Qinghe, and Shouhe. He married a woman née He. He ranked tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zongyi and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Rong. His grandfather, Pu, was a prefectural school instructor, posthumously granted the title Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His father, Mu, was a prefect and formerly Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His mother, née Bian, was granted the title Lady of Repose. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Xiao 季斆, courtesy name Yanwen, was registered in a civilian household in Rui’an County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-two, born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather, Chen, served as Police Chief; his father was Yi, and his mother was née Xiang. His parents were deceased. His younger brother was Tao. He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ju 汪舉, courtesy name Yongzhi, was registered in an official household in Xianghe County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongren; his grandfather, Shiyuan, was posthumously appointed Hanlin Academy Compiler; his father, Xie, was Right Vice Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Hanlin Academician and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites. His father’s former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady for Service; his mother, née Tang, was granted the same title. His mother alone survived. His elder brother, Deng, was a Secretariat Drafter, and his younger brother was Ci. He married a woman née He. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Xiao 滕霄, courtesy name Zichong, was registered in a military household of Jiyang Guard and was a native of Jian’an County, Fujian; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenshou; his grandfather was Yue; his father, Cong, was an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yun, Han, and Bin. He married a woman née Yan. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xian 汪獻, courtesy name Weixian, was registered in a military household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather was Min; his father was Xi; and his mother was née Xie. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Ji 䪠. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Xia. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

方天雨〔貫浙江嚴州府淳安縣官籍，國子生，治春秋，字濟甫，行一，年三十九，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖原仁，祖文傑〔封監察御史〕，父中〔按察司副使〕，母何氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，弟天敘、天民、天陟，娶周氏。浙江鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百九十九名。

呂夔〔貫江西廣信府永豐縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字祖邦，行七，年三十一，十一月二十日生〕。曾祖子榮〔封奉議大夫南京刑部郎中〕，祖晟〔知府，旌表孝子〕，父祥，嫡母俞氏，繼母姜氏。具慶下，弟龍、夷、益、皐，娶婁氏。江西鄉試第三十八名，會試第九名。
translation_en:
Xu Tianze, registered in a Guard household in Changping County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and an attached student of the Shuntian Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Huimin. Seventh in birth order, he was twenty-one years old and was born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Bo'ang; his grandfather was Lu; his father was Yun, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Que. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yi, and his younger brother was Tianheng. He married a woman née Pan. He ranked sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chu Nan, registered in a civilian household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guangyuan. Second in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Boji; his grandfather was Shi; his father was Xun; and his mother was née Yin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Nanming, and his younger brothers were Nanyun, Nanjin, and Nanyang. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked 133rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Tianyu, registered in an official household in Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jifu. First in birth order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanren; his grandfather was Wenjie, who received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; his father was Zhong, Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother was née He, who received the title of Lady. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Tianxu, Tianmin, and Tianzhi. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Kui, registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zubang. Seventh in birth order, he was thirty-one years old and was born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zirong, who received the honorary titles of Grand Master for Deliberation and Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Sheng, a Prefect officially commended for filial piety; his father was Xiang; his father's principal wife was née Yu; and his stepmother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Long, Yi, Yi, and Gao. He married a woman née Lou. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Shi, courtesy name Weike, was registered in a military household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshan; his grandfather, 𥜥 [?], was posthumously granted the title of Vice Prefect; and his father, Qing, was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His father’s former wife, née Xiao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Chen, a Commissioner; Ren, formerly a Secretariat Drafter; Shi, an honorary official; and Zhan, a government student. His younger brother was Bu. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Yuan. He ranked first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji, courtesy name Xunli, was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyong, his grandfather Taiqian, his father Shiguang, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xuntan, and he married a woman née Zeng. He ranked twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Gun, courtesy name Chaozhang, was registered in a military household of the Yingzhou Left Garrison Guard and was a native of Shangyu County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junzhang; his grandfather, Hao, was posthumously granted the title of Guard Registrar; and his father, Hui, was a Guard Registrar. His mother, née Zhong, was posthumously granted the title of Lady, and his stepmother, née Chai, was granted the title of Lady. His father and stepmother were both living. His younger brother was Pao, and he married a woman née Zheng. He ranked 130th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Guan, courtesy name Cuncheng, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duanjing, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Fengyi. His father’s former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Yue. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Cheng, and he married a woman née He. He ranked eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

章寓之〔貫四川嘉定州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字道充，行一，年三十四，五月初三日生〕。曾祖潮，祖立宗，父端，母劉氏。具慶下，弟完之、寛之，娶辛氏。四川鄉試第六十五名，會試第九十二名。

胡軒〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣軍籍，儒士，治禮記，字士榮，行一，年三十三，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖達，祖禮，父楷，母孫氏。慈侍下，弟轅、範、輔，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百三十五名。

李津〔貫廣東肇慶府四會縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字濟之，行一，年四十，十一月三十日生〕。曾祖宗林〔知縣〕，祖克，父金〔前典史〕，前母梁氏、陳氏，母羅氏。具慶下，弟注、泮，娶廖氏。廣東鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百七十四名。
translation_en:
Ouyang Gao, registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was Instructor at the county Confucian school in Macheng, Huguang. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Cizhi. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongren; his grandfather was Guangjun, granted the honorary cap and girdle under provisions for imperial favor; his father was Ning, an Admonisher; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Shi, Rang (a County Magistrate), and Xun. His wife was née Luo. He placed thirty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuzhi, registered in a military household in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Daochong. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chao; his grandfather was Lizong; his father was Duan; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wanzhi and Kuanzhi, and his wife was née Xin. He placed sixty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xuan, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shirong. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da; his grandfather was Li; his father was Kai; and his mother was née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yuan, Fan, and Fu, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jin, registered in a civilian household in Sihui County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jizhi. First in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zonglin, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Ke; and his father was Jin, formerly a County Clerk. His father’s former wives were née Liang and née Chen; his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhu and Pan, and his wife was née Liao. He placed thirty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yong, courtesy name Erxi, was registered in an official household of Changling Guard and was a native of Linhuai County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang, posthumously awarded the titles General Who Cherishes the Distant and Vice Commander of a Guard; his grandfather was Yun; his father was Gui; and his mother was née Hu. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brother was Chang. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked 103rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Zhi, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was eighth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Daoyong; his grandfather was Jingxu; his father was Kun; and his mother was née Shao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Long, and he married a woman née Li. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yijun, courtesy name Bingheng, was registered in a civilian household in Linshui County, Guang'an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Sicong; his grandfather was Fu, posthumously awarded the title Investigating Censor; and his father was Chun, Vice Surveillance Commissioner. His legal mother was née Tang, granted the title Lady, and his birth mother was née Liu. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Wanjun, Qianjun, and Baijun, each an honorary official, and Shijun. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Xun, courtesy name Tingfang, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yanzheng; his grandfather was Li; his father was En; his mother was née Zhang; and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian and Ne, and he married a woman née Li. He ranked sixty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Shixiu, courtesy name Rushi, was registered in a military household of Fengyi Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Guixian County, Xunzhou Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Hui; and his father, Bin, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiju, and his younger brothers were Shimin and Shijia. His wife was née Huang. He placed fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chou, courtesy name Yunsheng, was registered with Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Xingan County, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wanbin; his grandfather, Wang; and his father, Tong. His mother was née Tian. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ren, and his wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yue, courtesy name Yizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Jun, posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; and his father, Mao, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Ye, Wan, and Yimei [?]. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Jin, courtesy name Meizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Linying County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxing; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Li, Assistant Gentleman for Rendering Service. His mother was née Zhao. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ming, and his younger brother was Qin. His wife was née Zhao. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李貫〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字志道，行五，年二十七，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖肄，祖璠，父杲議，母莊氏。重慶下，兄珏、璵、冑、翱，娶武氏，繼娶賈氏。福建鄉試第四十名，會試第二百五十六名。

translation_en:
Xu Lin, registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and originally from Longyou County, Zhejiang, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Renbo; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tianzhi, his grandfather Wenhe, and his father Shun; his father's former wife was Lady Li, his mother Lady Yang, and his stepmother Lady Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Luan, and he married Lady Hu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Guan, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhidao; he ranked fifth in his family and was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Fan, his father Gaoyi [?], and his mother Lady Zhuang. His parents and grandparent or grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jue, Yu, Zhou, and Ao. He married Lady Wu and subsequently Lady Jia. He placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jian, registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenshun; he ranked thirty-ninth in his family and was thirty-eight, born on the third day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yingxiang, his grandfather Yu, his father Kai, and his mother Lady Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ru, and he married Lady Zhu. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Shiqi, registered in a military household in Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Yuan was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His grandfather Su was an Instructor, granted the title Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works, and posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His father Wen held the titles Grand Master for Rectitude and Governor for Aid in Governance and served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel. His mother, Lady Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Virtue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother Shicong was a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Shixian, a tribute scholar, Shiming, an Instructor of Medicine, Shijie, and Shixun. He married Lady Jia and subsequently Lady Li. He placed forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

畢濟川〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字汝舟，行六十九，年三十四，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖德興，祖淵〔國子生，贈工部主事〕，父瑜〔按察司提學僉事〕，母方氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟濟時〔貢士〕、濟民，娶江氏。江西鄉試第二名，會試第四名。

translation_en:
Huang Yuegu, courtesy name Shizhun, was a National University student registered in a civilian household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked third in family birth order, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Ji was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather Shouyi was a Registrar; and his father Jie held the privilege of wearing official cap and belt. His father's principal wife was née Li, and his birth mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jigu and Shigu, and his wife was née Yuan. He placed sixty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zhou, courtesy name Pinghou, was a National University student registered in a civilian household in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. He specialized in the Book of Rites, ranked third in family birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Yifang was an Instructor; his grandfather Qiansheng was a National University student; his father was Zheng; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mian and Liu, and his wife was née Zhong. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bi Jichuan, courtesy name Ruzhou, was a National University student registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked sixty-ninth in family birth order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Dexing. His grandfather Yuan was a National University student posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works. His father Yu was an Education Intendant serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Provincial Surveillance Commission. His mother, née Fang, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Jishi, a tribute scholar, and Jimin; his wife was née Jiang. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Xun, courtesy name Chengzhi, was a National University student registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked third in family birth order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chiwen; his grandfather was Shile; his father was Shangzheng; his mother was née Guo; and his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ke and Kui, and his younger brothers were Zao, Bo, and Qing. His wife was née Peng. He placed eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Yingjing, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dezheng; he ranked fourteenth in family birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sizhi, his grandfather Zhongqian, his father Ang, and his mother Lady Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hao, Hui, Can, Fan, and Yinglü; his younger brother was Yingqi. He married Lady Yang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Gao, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingzhao; he ranked second in family birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Fu 敷, his father Fu 輔, an Assistant Prefect, and his mother Lady Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sheng. He married Lady Xu. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Timin; he ranked fourth in family birth order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongbin, his grandfather Simin, a Subprefect, his father Wenkui, and his mother Lady Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lin, a District Magistrate, Feng, and Lian. He married Lady Wang 汪. He placed twenty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nahui, registered in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xianke; he ranked first in family birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fengxian, a Registrar, his grandfather Duo, his father Cong, an Instructor, and his mother Lady Xu. Both parents were living. He married Lady Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

何瑭〔貫河南懷慶衛軍籍，直隸如皋縣人，河内縣學生，治詩經，字粹夫，行一，年二十九，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖貴，祖濱，父森，母劉氏。具慶下，弟璋，娶周氏。河南鄉試第一名，會試第十六名。

戴敔〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，廣東新會縣學教諭，治禮記，字廷韶，行一，年三十七，正月十六日生〕。曾祖文週，祖弘昭，父昂〔教授〕，母陳氏。永感下，兄孜、政、敦，弟牧、廣、畋，娶林氏。福建鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百一名。

translation_en:
He Tang, registered in a military household of Huaiqing Guard, Henan, and a native of Rugao County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Henei County school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Cuifu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Bin, his father Sen, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living, his younger brother was Zhang, and his wife was née Zhou; he placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Lun, registered in a civilian household of Linshui County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingzhong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was forty-two, born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bicong, his grandfather Guang, his father Wenli, a Registrar, and his mother née Tao; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Yi, and his younger brothers were Ren, Reng, Yan, Qiao, and Ai; he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently women née Bai and née Li, and placed eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Yu, registered in a civilian household of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was Instructor at the Xinhui County school in Guangdong, specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Tingshao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhou, his grandfather Hongzhao, his father Ang, a Professor, and his mother née Chen; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Zi, Zheng, and Dun, his younger brothers were Mu, Guang, and Tian, and his wife was née Lin; he placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Siyi, registered in a civilian household of Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jixian, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shirong, his grandfather Lun, his father Feng, and his mother née Yin; his grandparents and parents were living, his younger brothers were Sipu, Sizhen, Sisui, and Sibao, and his wife was née Liu; he placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
謝廷瑞〔貫福建福州府長樂縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字邦應，行八，年四十，正月初五日生。〕曾祖琬，祖孟安〔封太，父士穆，前母陳氏，母潘氏，繼母梁氏。〕具慶下，兄廷秀〔貢士〕、廷柱〔大理寺右評事〕，弟廷正、廷棐、廷最、廷衮、廷豐，娶林氏。福建鄉試第三名，會試第一百二十八名。

歐陽禄〔貫湖廣永州府道州永明縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字萬鍾，行十一，年三十四，七月二十六日生。〕曾祖均羨，祖崇禮，父奎〔知縣〕，母毛氏。慈侍下，兄祚、禕、袪、裕，娶蔣氏。湖廣鄉試第四十九名，會試第二十五名。

程雲鵬〔貫四川順慶府南充縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字文南，行一，年二十六，四月二十九日生。〕曾祖天佑，祖賢〔縣丞〕，父宗傑，母杜氏。重慶下，弟雲鳳、雲鶚、雲鵾、雲龍，娶文氏。四川鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百十名。

王金〔貫河南開封府許州臨潁縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字曰良，行一，年三十二，九月二十七日生。〕曾祖睿〔知州〕，祖璽〔判官〕，父相，母邢氏，繼母潘氏。具慶下，弟玉、迹、業、休，娶李氏。河南鄉試第六十六名，會試第二百四十一名。
translation_en:
Xie Tingrui, courtesy name Bangying, was registered in a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was eighth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wan; his grandfather was Meng'an, whose honorary title is garbled as “tai” [?]; and his father was Shimu. His father's former wife was née Chen, his mother née Pan, and his stepmother née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingxiu, a tribute scholar, and Tingzhu, Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his younger brothers were Tingzheng, Tingfei, Tingzui, Tinggun, and Tingfeng. His wife was née Lin. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Lu, courtesy name Wanzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yongming County, Dao Subprefecture, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was eleventh in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Junxian; his grandfather was Chongli; his father was Kui, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Mao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zuo, Yi, Qu, and Yu, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed forty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Yunpeng, courtesy name Wennan, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Tianyou; his grandfather was Xian, an Assistant District Magistrate; his father was Zongjie; and his mother was née Du. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yunfeng, Yun'e, Yunkun, and Yunlong, and his wife was née Wen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin, courtesy name Yueliang, was registered in a civilian household in Linying County, Xu Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rui, a Subprefect; his grandfather was Xi, an Administrative Assistant; his father was Xiang; his mother was née Xing; and his stepmother was née Pan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Ji, Ye, and Xiu, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

汪鋐〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字宣之，行四，年三十七，九月十八日生〕。曾祖濟川，祖希文，父儼〔前教諭〕，母李氏。重慶下，兄銃，弟鉉、鍪、錠，娶程氏。應天府鄉試第九十六名，會試第九十三名。

盛鍾〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣軍籍，長洲縣人，崑山縣學增廣生，治易經，字秀甫，行三，年二十九，六月初五日生〕。曾祖彥敬，祖景昌，父箴〔訓導〕，前母董氏、朱氏，母穆氏。慈侍下，兄經、緯，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第四十一名，會試第一百七十八名。
translation_en:
Ma Wen, registered in a military household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shimei; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Weiliang, his grandfather Tianrong, and his father Jing, an Assistant Prefect. His father's principal wife was née Cao, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yuan, and his younger brother Kang (annotation: “guan yi” [?]). His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yun Wei, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongfu; he ranked sixth in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Kerang, his grandfather Bian, officially commended as a righteous commoner, and his father Ao, granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations. His father's former wife was née Jiang, his mother was née Xie, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yan, Cen, Duan, Zhuan, Yong, and Chong; his younger brother was Ba. His wife was née Xiao. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hong, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xuanzhi; he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jichuan, his grandfather Xiwen, and his father Yan, a former Instructor. His mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Chong; his younger brothers were Xuan, Mou, and Ding. His wife was née Cheng. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Zhong, registered in a military household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Changzhou County and was an added-quota student at the Kunshan County school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yanjing, his grandfather Jingchang, and his father Zhen, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wives were née Dong and née Zhu, and his mother was née Mu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jing and Wei. His wife was née Jin. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ye Fengling, registered in a military household in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was Instructor at the county school of Xingan, Jiangxi; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Changshao, ranked eighth among his brothers, and was aged forty-two, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanshi, his grandfather Zhiyuan, and his father Zhe; his father's principal wife was née Chen, and his birth mother was née He. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Long, Kun, Ao, E, Lin, Zhang, and Xiang; his younger brothers were Zhan, Qi, Hui, Yi, and Yue. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Zhao, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county-school student; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Shimian, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benhua, his grandfather Qing, and his father Wei; his mother was née Xiong and his stepmother née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ming and Tie, and his wife was née Xiong. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Bin, registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county-school student; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Xuezhi, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizheng, his grandfather Xing, and his father Jie; his mother was née Ye. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brother was Huan and his younger brother Bian. His wife was née Cheng; he subsequently married a woman née Hu. He placed 127th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tianqi, registered in a military officer household of the Guilin Right Guard, Guangxi, was an Imperial University student; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Renzheng, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Cong, and his father Feng; his mother was née Xing. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brother was Tianxiang; his younger brothers were Tianjuan (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Tianxi (an Assistant Instructor), Tianhe, Tianqiu, and Tianlin. His wife was née Liang. He placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xiandao, registered in a civilian household in Yanshan County, Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Weizhi; he was fourth among his brothers, aged forty-five, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanlu; his grandfather, Cong, was a Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; his father was Wen, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hongdao, an Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Zongdao, and Youdao; his younger brothers were Ningdao, a Vice Commissioner of a granary, Zhidao, and Lidao. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Wenjie, registered in a civilian household in Changting County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bangchen; he was third among his brothers, aged twenty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hesheng; his grandfather, Qing, was a County Clerk; his father, Zheng, had been sentenced to military service at Rehe Guard [?] and subsequently permitted under an applicable regulation to wear official cap and girdle. His mother, née Lai, was granted the title of Senior Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Qi and Wenjun, the latter a Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his younger brothers were Wenwei and Wenhui. His wife was née Xu. He ranked tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zong, registered in a warrior household of the Tengxiang Left Guard and a native of Yishi County, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Weiben; he was fifth among his brothers, aged thirty-eight, and born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Sili; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Chen, and his mother was née He. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xi, Ning, a Prefectural Records Keeper, Hong, and Yu. His wife was née Jing; he subsequently married a woman née Fan. He ranked 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bingqing, registered in a military household of Yongping Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanliang; he was first among his brothers, aged thirty-six, and born on the second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather was Zheng; his father, Tinggang, was a Messenger. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Bingzhong. His wife was née Xiao; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Ting 林烶, courtesy name Tingguang, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-eight sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Tao; his father was Ji, a National University student; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan, Xi, Wei, and Lang, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Jun 廖俊, courtesy name Dezhang, was registered as a guardsman in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Xingan County, Jiangxi; a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-seven sui, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. Zheng Xin 鄭信, courtesy name Defu, was registered in a military household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sanshe, his grandfather Gui, his father Guan, Assistant Judicial Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, and his mother née Suo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ren and Lun, his younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wei 楊瑋, courtesy name Jingqi, was registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong; a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-seven sui, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin, his grandfather Chongyi, his father Tingguang, and his mother née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ying and Tian; he married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zidao. Twelfth in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His elder brothers were Tiqin, an Instructor, and □□fang [?], a District Magistrate. His wife was née Ou. He placed eighty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Guo, registered in Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shifu. Fifth in birth order, he was twenty-seven years old, born on the thirtieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chucai, his grandfather Lan, and his father Jin; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Gai. His wife was née Zhao. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Huan, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jihe. Third in birth order, he was thirty years old, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin, his grandfather Xianzong, and his father Dehua. His father's principal wife was née Zhao, his stepmother was née Gu, and his birth mother was née Hu. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi and Yi, and his younger brother was Heng. His wife was née Xia. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yuankui, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, a Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Tianze; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuanbi, and he was betrothed to a woman née Lao. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Hao, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenhan; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty, born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianshi; his grandfather was Ying; and his father was Jian, who had been granted the privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations. His father's former wife was née Ji, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chun and Pu, the latter an Assistant Instructor. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Xueshu, registered in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongzhong; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yande; his grandfather was Cheng, an Honorary Official; his father was Xun, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Xiong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xuesi and his younger brother was Xueshi. He married a woman née Xiong and subsequently a woman née Tan. He placed seventy-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiuchou, registered in Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuxue; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Gui, a Chief of Police; his father was Gang; and his mother was née Sun. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His younger brother was Jiusi, and he married a woman née Dong. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yun 王雲, registered in a military household in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Tianzhang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xilu, his grandfather Shun, his father Tong, and his mother née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ni and Ji, and his wife was née Dou. He ranked ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xuan 陳炫, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenguang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyuan, his grandfather Jiang, his father Yi, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhao, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked sixty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Min 祁敏, registered in a military household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Weixue; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhenzong; his grandfather Binggang was posthumously awarded the title of Vice Director; and his father Shun was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His legal mother, née Zhong, was posthumously awarded the title of Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Liao, and his birth mother née Liang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xiao 斆, Zi 孜, Zheng 政, Xiao 敩, and Dun 敦; the two names written 斆 and 敩 appear to be variant forms of the same character [?]. His wife was née Li. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yi 丁沂, registered in a military household in Lishui County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zonglu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu, his grandfather Yong, his father Xi, and his mother née Duan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Han, Si, Jun, and Pan, and his wife was née Yuan. He ranked eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Song Mian, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a salt-producing household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Kongzhan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five [?], born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongcheng, his grandfather Tingfang, his father Xuan, and his mother née Huang; his grandparents and parents were living; his elder brother was Guan and his younger brothers were Gun, Yi, and Bian; he married a woman née Xiang and subsequently a woman née Xu; he placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Ao, registered in a military household of the Nanjing Left Yulin Guard and a native of Danyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenji, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Sheng, his father Shun, and his mother née Guo; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Luan and Jian; he married a woman née Wang; he placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hui, registered in Pinggu County, Ji Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, in a military household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruji, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bi, his grandfather Yun (Prefect), his father Zhu (Associate Prefect), his mother née Li, and his successive stepmothers née Wu and née Wang; his father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brother was You and his younger brothers were Yue (Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue), Zuo, Zhi, and Xia; he married a woman née Hu; he placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bian, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingyan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Xuan, his father Yuan, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Yu; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Mao, Huan, and Mo; he married a woman née Ru and subsequently a woman née Du; he placed fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

項匡〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣，民籍，順天府順義縣學教諭，治詩經，字直卿，行六，年三十七，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖德中，祖彥遠，父文達，母李氏，繼母張氏。具慶下，兄滂、麒、轍、源、澄，弟麟、浩，娶周氏。浙江鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百六十三名。

康紀〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字在脩，行三，年三十五，二月二十六日生〕。曾祖宜順〔贈監察御史〕，祖弘敬〔按察司僉事〕，父文秀，母歐陽氏，繼母羅氏。重慶下，兄純、綬，弟紳、綽、綏、編、綍，娶王氏。江西鄉試第三十九名，會試第一百七十一名。
translation_en:
Third Class: 199 men, granted the status of having the same background as metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Bian Simin, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shuqi, his grandfather Ji, and his father Zixian; his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sixue and Siwen, and his wife was née Sun. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Kuang, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. He was Instructor at the county school of Shunyi, Shuntian Prefecture, and specialized in the Classic of Poetry; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dezhong, his grandfather Yanyuan, and his father Wenda; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Pang, Qi, Zhe, Yuan, and Cheng, and his younger brothers were Lin and Hao; his wife was née Zhou. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Ji, courtesy name Zaixiu, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Changes; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yishun, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Hongjing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father was Wenxiu. His mother was née Ouyang and his stepmother née Luo. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Chun and Shou, and his younger brothers were Shen, Chuo, Sui, Bian, and Fu; his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳鉞〔貫江西撫州府崇仁縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字宿威，行九，年三十，四月二十四日生〕。曾祖日昇〔贈順天府治中〕，祖衡〔布政司參議〕，父孜〔前翰林院典籍〕，嫡母諶氏，生母趙氏。重慶下，弟鎬、錫，娶劉氏，繼娶甘氏。江西鄉試第八名，會試第一百四十七名。

張龍〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，醫籍，國子生，治書經，字汝言，行二，年三十三，七月二十三日生〕。曾祖逢吉〔御醫，贈中書舍人〕，祖𦐇〔尚寶司卿〕，父慶〔光祿寺丞〕，前母潘氏，嫡母曾氏，生母顧氏。具慶下，兄夔，弟稷、契、臯、岳，娶何氏。順天府鄉試第六十一名，會試第五十六名。

林茂達〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字孚可，行三，年四十一，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖應鳳，祖珪〔訓導，贈知州〕，父思承〔府同知〕，母黃氏〔封宜人〕，繼母鄭氏。慈侍下，兄茂榮、茂春〔陰陽官〕，娶柯氏。福建鄉試第十七名，會試第四十八名。
translation_en:
Cai Quan, registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xuanzhi. Seventh in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenshan, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Yongyi; his father was Xun; and his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Duo, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Qin, Ming, Yue, and Yong. He married a woman née Ma. He ranked seventy-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yue, registered in Chongren County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Suwei. Ninth in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Risheng, posthumously granted the title of Administrative Assistant of Shuntian Prefecture; his grandfather was Heng, an Assistant Administration Commissioner; and his father was Zi, formerly Librarian of the Hanlin Academy. His legal mother was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Zhao. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Hao and Xi. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Gan. He ranked eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Long, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a medical household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruyan. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Fengji, an Imperial Physician posthumously granted the title of Secretariat Drafter; his grandfather was Ta (𦐇) [?], Chief Minister of the Office of Imperial Seals; and his father was Qing, Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His father's former wife was née Pan, his legal mother was née Zeng, and his birth mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Ji, Qi, Gao, and Yue. He married a woman née He. He ranked sixty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Maoda, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Fuke. Third in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yingfeng; his grandfather was Gui, an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Department Magistrate; and his father was Sicheng, a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His mother was née Huang, granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren), and his stepmother was née Zheng. His mother was living, but his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Maorong and Maochun, the latter an official of astronomy and calendrical studies. He married a woman née Ke. He ranked seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.
