translation_en:
Yuwen Zhong, courtesy name Boxiu, was registered in a military household [?] in Qianzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yuci County, Shanxi; he specialized in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Heng, and his father Jing, a judge; his mother was Lady Zhou and his stepmother Lady Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yong and Xu. He married Lady Xu and subsequently Lady Xue. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Cha, courtesy name Yuanxi, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region; he was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked eighteenth in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jifang, his grandfather Xuan, his father Ji, and his mother Lady Tan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xuan, Ning, Bao (Investigating Censor), and Bin (annotated “learning of the mind” [?]); his younger brother was Huan. He married Lady Wang and subsequently Lady Zhang. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Ao, courtesy name Zhenqing, was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wujiang County in the Metropolitan Region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuangsun, his grandfather Jin, his father Xiang, and his mother Lady Pang. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married Lady Bi. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Lun, courtesy name Dajing, was registered in a military household of the Shence Guard and was a native of Shenzhou in the Metropolitan Region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Jing, his father Xiang, and his mother Lady Jia. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jin, Hong, and Shao. He married Lady Li. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Duan Zhi, courtesy name Shigao, was registered in a military household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Zezhou, Shanxi. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fengxian; his grandfather, Shan, received the honorary title of Investigating Censor and the posthumous title of Prefect; his father, Zheng, was Grand Master of the Palace (dazhong dafu) and Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Jiao. He placed fifteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yi, courtesy name Shiyi, was registered in a military household of Zhuolu Left Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuliu; his grandfather, Zhongren; and his father, Hai. His father's former wife was née Gu; his legal mother was née Chen; his stepmother, née Han; and his birth mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, Xiang, and Xin. He married a woman née Zhai. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chen, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a military household of Xi'an Front Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yichuan County, Yan'an Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian; his grandfather, Yuan; and his father, Jun. His father's former wife was née Zhao; his mother was née Wu; and his stepmother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yan, a County Magistrate, Jin, Xi, and Tian; his younger brother was Wen, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan). He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Duo, courtesy name Wenzhen, was registered in a military household of Funing County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zi; his grandfather, Jing, was Commissioner of a Tax Office; his father was Hai; and his mother was née Xing. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jun. He married a woman née Qiao and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yuanji, registered in a military household in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shouzheng; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Xiong, an administrative judge; and his mother, née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother, Yuanheng, held the honorary title of Righteous Official. He married a woman née Hu. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Yue, registered in a military household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bingqian; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xixian; his grandfather, Bin; his father, Jun; and his mother, née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Ying, and Rong, and his younger brother was Zhao. He married a woman née Wang, then successively women née Luo and Dang. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huo En, registered in an officer household of Maoshan Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission, was a native of Yizhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His educational status is given as “school” [?], and he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianxi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather, Wang, grandfather, Jing, and father, Yun, were each battalion commanders. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Zhao. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shu and Tianjue. He married a woman née Lan, subsequently married a woman née Cui, and was later betrothed to a woman née Liu. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bi, registered in an officer household of the Nanjing Embroidered-Uniform Guard, was a native of Huayin County, Shaanxi, and a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bangzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yizhu, a company commander; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Xiang; and his mother, née Mei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong, a company commander, and Fu. He married a woman née Bei. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉經〔貫山東東昌府高唐州恩縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字貞甫，行一，年三十九，六月二十一日生〕。曾祖定，祖逸〔主簿〕，父瑛，前母程氏，母徐氏。嚴侍下，弟紳，娶雷氏。山東鄉試第二十八名，會試第一百五十八名。
translation_en:
Zhou Zhen, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tianzhao, and he ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Yongcai, and his father Tingze (the annotation 官義 may mean an honorary official [?]); his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Yu, Ti, Zuo, and Yi. His wife was née Qin. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Kui, registered in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruxie, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Xian, and his father Shao (Gentleman for Rendering Service); his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Rui (a commoner honored for righteousness), and his younger brothers were Fan, Jin, and Zao. His wife was née Rui. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Xian, registered in Wenshui County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zungu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingming, his grandfather Ji, and his father Duo; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xian. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jing, registered in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhenfu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Yi (Registrar), and his father Ying. His father's former wife was née Cheng, and his mother was née Xu. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Shen. His wife was née Lei. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cheng Wen 成文, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a military household of the Shanyin Battalion in Shanxi and was a native of Wenshui County, Taiyuan Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jing, his father Ben, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiu, and his younger brothers were Ji and Jin. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married women née Wang and Wang [the repeated surname is uncertain: ?]. He placed forty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Siming 武思明, courtesy name Kecheng, was registered in a civilian household in Lingchuan County, Zezhou, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan; his grandfather He was officially commended as a righteous commoner; and his father Ning held honorary official status for charitable service. His father's former wives were née Li and née Ji, and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Sixian also held honorary official status for charitable service; his younger brothers were Sigong, Sixiao, Sijing, and Siyi. He married a woman née Ji. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Sicheng 白思誠, courtesy name Shizhi, was registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xun was an Adjudicator; his grandfather Qi received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father Yi held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father's former wife was née Sun, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Siming, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Siyi, a Subprefect; and Siwen, an Administrative Assistant. His younger brother was Side. He married a woman née Yan. He placed forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xuan 鄭選, courtesy name Yuzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Guangzhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xian was a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Hong; and his father Zan was a government-stipend student. His mother was née Dan, and his stepmother was née Gong. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Qian. He married a woman née Lan. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Xiang, registered in Gao’an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yinghe. First in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qixin; his grandfather, Fangyu; and his father, Yong, a prefectural Confucian school instructor. His mother was née Xie. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhen, Xi (a tribute student), Zhi, Tuo [?], Pao [?], Pou [?], and Qiu [?]. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Jin, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a county Confucian school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yili. Third in birth order, he was forty-seven years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his grandfather, Yuntong [?]; and his father, Fuqing. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Cai and Kui. He married a woman née Dai and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Qin, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingzhi. Seventh in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu; his grandfather, Shiheng; and his father, Bing. His mother was née Weng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yin (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), Bo, and Kai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tingxiang, registered in Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was originally from Luzhou, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bingheng. First in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siyi; his grandfather, Shi; and his father, Zeng. His mother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tingwu. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

危行〔貫福建邵武府邵武縣匠籍，國子生，治書經，字世隆，行二，年三十九，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖原宗，祖仲達，父伯實，母官氏。永感下，兄泰，弟璧、讓，娶蘇氏。福建鄉試第六十四名，會試第一百二十四名。

姚鵬〔貫浙江嘉興府崇德縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字鳴南，行八，年二十九，二月十二日生〕。曾祖孟謙，祖璣〔恩例冠帶〕，父澯，母俞氏。重慶下，兄楷、鳳〔貢士〕、鸞，弟鵾、鷺、鸘，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第六十五名，會試第八十七名。

江淙〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字朝會，行十，年四十，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖永崇，祖序泂，父益德，母席氏。具慶下，弟湍，娶劉氏。江西鄉試第二名，會試第十四名。
translation_en:
Wei Xing 危行, courtesy name Shilong, was registered in an artisan household in Shaowu County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in family order and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanzong; his grandfather, Zhongda; his father, Boshi; and his mother, née Guan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tai, and his younger brothers were Bi and Rang. His wife was née Su. He placed sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xuezeng 李學曽, courtesy name Zonglu, was registered in a civilian household in Maoming County, Gaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the intercalary sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fushou, a county-school Instructor; his grandfather, Keyou, a tribute student (gongshi); his father, Cai; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuemeng, Xueyao, Xueshen, Xuelian, Xuezhu, and Xuesi. His wife was née Wang. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Peng 姚鵬, courtesy name Mingnan, was registered in a civilian household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth in family order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengqian; his grandfather, Ji, who had been granted the honorary privilege of wearing an official cap and girdle under provisions of imperial grace; his father, Can; and his mother, née Yu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Kai, Feng (a tribute student), and Luan; his younger brothers were Kun, Lu, and Shuang. His wife was née Shen. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Cong 江淙, courtesy name Chaohui, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked tenth in family order and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchong; his grandfather, Xujiong; his father, Yide; and his mother, née Xi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tuan. His wife was née Liu. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yun 張雲, courtesy name Jisheng, was registered in an official household of Xinyang Guard, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Dechun and grandfather Ao were company commanders; his father was He, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhen. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zi Shou 訾綬, courtesy name Wenfu, was registered in a military household in Shuozhou, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, and was originally from Shenmu County, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather was Rong, his father was Yu, a county school instructor, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhen, Lun, and Jin. He married a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wen 徐問, courtesy name Yongzhong, was registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather was Yi, his father was Wang [?], and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xue, and his younger brothers were Si and Bian. He was betrothed to a woman née Chu. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Cai 王材, courtesy name Tiancheng, was registered in a medical household in Wangjiang County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhenlong, his grandfather was Min, his father was Qiong, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Qi and Song, both honorary officials; his younger brothers were Jia, Kai, Huan, Yue, Gan, an instructor of medicine, Chun, a literary official [?], Li, an honorary official, Nan, and Luan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Jin, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jianqing; he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins, was forty sui, and was born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lida; his grandfather, Zhineng; his father, Xinjia, a Bureau Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War; and his mother, née Liu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun, and Hui, and his younger brother was Shen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shangguan Chong, registered in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Daqing; he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-six sui, and was born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhicheng; his grandfather, Yonglu; his father, Xingxian; his mother, née Luo; and his stepmother, née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Song and Wei. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Bangzhu, registered in Cangwu County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Anguo; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-six sui, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangli; his grandfather, Yongguang; and his father, Zhen. His father’s former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Gan. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Ruan and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed seventh in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Shilin, registered in Cangwu County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhaozhou; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-nine sui, and was born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youquan; his grandfather, Tonghai, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his father, Jizong, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shifeng and Shilong, both tribute scholars (gongshi), and Shi’ao and Shixiong. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventeenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Rong, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked nineteenth in birth order and was thirty-five sui, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenju; his grandfather, Weishan; his father, Da, held a prestige title; and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhu and Sen, and his younger brothers were Kai, Xiao, Tang, Huai, Quan, Bing, and Ben. His wife was née Ni. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Jun, courtesy name Keming, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingshun; his grandfather, Wenjian; his father, Chang; his mother was née Huang, and his stepmother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His wife was née Yang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Heqing, courtesy name Yingqi, was registered in a civilian household in Nan'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-five sui, born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianlin; his grandfather, Bo; his father, Tianxi; and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Liuqing, Chengqing, Hanqing, and Shuqing. His wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Chi, courtesy name Jiazheng, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked seventh in birth order and was thirty-three sui, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qisheng; his grandfather, Tianhua, was posthumously granted the title of Registrar; his father was Wende; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, an Assistant Instructor, and Jian; his younger brothers were Qin and Jin. His wife was née Luo. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yuanchun, courtesy name Youren, was registered in a medical household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Can, a Physician; his grandfather was Sheng, a Physician advanced to the prestige rank of Gentleman for Cultivated Service (xiuzhilang); and his father was Rui, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions (yiguan). His mother was née Mei, and his stepmother née Gao. His grandfather and parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuanjiao, Yuanxiang, Yuanxun, Yuanbi, Yuanlong, and Yuanmei. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Ye, courtesy name Yaoqing, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Zheng, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; and his father was Yue. His mother was née Pan. His grandfather and parents were living. His younger brother was Bing, and he married a woman née Mei. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Fan, courtesy name Bangzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiwen, his grandfather Hui, and his father Tao. His mother was née Zhou, and his stepmother née Chi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was You, and he married a woman née Jia. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Qiong, courtesy name Shangde, was registered in a household of picked warriors of the Wuxiang Right Guard and was a native of Changxing County, Zhejiang. An added-quota student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiwen, his grandfather Zongdao, and his father Fu, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Wei. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Xuan and his younger brother Yuan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Qi, registered in an official household under the Disciplinary Office of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingfeng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Anshan; his grandfather, Zheng, was a Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his father, Hong, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née He, had been granted the title Lady. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Kun, a metropolitan graduate in the same examination year; Xiu, a Battalion Disciplinary Officer in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; and Min. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhu, registered in a military household in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yucheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yunning; his grandfather, Liang, held an honorary title for longevity; his father, Cong, was a Department Magistrate; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qi, who held an honorary title for public beneficence; Huai, a Registrar; and Ze, a County Vice Magistrate. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eighty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tinghuai, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was the son of an Assistant Instructor at the Yongfeng County Confucian School in Jiangxi [?] and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenxiang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the thirtieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongqian; his grandfather, Cong, was a Registrar; his father, Hongyong, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Weng. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mei Ke, registered in a civilian household in Wuhu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county Confucian school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bangzhen; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Sui; his father was Kai; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhu and Rui. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Jun, registered in Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Zhongyuan, ranked eleventh among his brothers and male cousins, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather, Qiguang, held an honorary longevity title; his father was Gao; his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother née Zhao. His father alone was still living. His elder brother was Hui, and his wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bu, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Shifu, ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, an Assistant Commissioner; his grandfather was Zheng; his father was Chuan; and his mother was née Qian. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Su, his younger brothers were Du and Heng, and his wife was née Huang. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Rujing, registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Gongpu, ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins, and was aged twenty-five, born on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Luan, a Prefectural Registrar; and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shan, his younger brother was Ruji, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Zhu, registered in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Kecheng, ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixin; his grandfather was Zhongquan; his father was Xi; and his mother was née Yan. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Zhi, Hao, Jing, and Kai, and his wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
張潤〔貫山西平陽府臨汾縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝霖，行二，年三十三，十月十一日生〕。曾祖仲實，祖祥，父鏞〔典史〕，母韓氏。具慶下，兄滋，弟灌，娶喬氏。山西鄉試第一名，會試第二百六十九名。

朱絃〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字廷和，行九，年三十三，二月十六日生〕。曾祖仲南，祖轅，父搢，母王氏。具慶下，兄鳥、珮、瑀、羙、璟、袞、瓛、錦，弟欽、紌、紳，娶嚴氏。應天府鄉試第七十四名，會試第二百五十五名。

范嵩〔貫福建建寧府甌寧縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字邦秀，行二，年三十二，十月初一日生〕。曾祖直，祖保，父澄〔監生〕，母吳氏。具慶下，兄山，弟嶽、崑、巖、岌，娶唐氏。福建鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百十四名。

曾直〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔溫，行三，年三十六，八月二十九日生〕。曾祖學忠〔贈監察御史〕，祖昌元，父光熈，母周氏。慈侍下，兄柔，弟簡，娶彭氏，繼娶許氏。江西鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百四十三名。
translation_en:
Zhang Run 張潤, courtesy name Rulin, was registered in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongshi; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Yong, a Clerk; and his mother, née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zi and his younger brother, Guan. He married a woman née Qiao. He ranked first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xian 朱絃, courtesy name Tinghe, was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongnan; his grandfather, Yuan; his father, Jin; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Niao [?], Pei, Yu, Mei, Jing, Gun, Huan, and Jin; his younger brothers were Qin, Qiu, and Shen. He married a woman née Yan. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Song 范嵩, courtesy name Bangxiu, was registered in Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Bao; his father, Cheng, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shan; his younger brothers were Yue, Kun, Yan, and Ji. He married a woman née Tang. He ranked sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Zhi 曾直, courtesy name Shuwen, was registered in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuezhong, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Changyuan; his father, Guangxi; and his mother, née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brother was Rou and his younger brother, Jian. He married a woman née Peng and subsequently a woman née Xu. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Yan, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was affiliated with the county school (status illegible: □□) and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Juzheng; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benchu; his grandfather, Lu, had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his father was Qiong, and his mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninetieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Kai, registered in an official household in Dingliao Central Guard, Liaodong, was a native of Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shujin; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Zhong, and father, Ji, were both Company Commanders. His mother was née Huang, and his successive stepmothers were née Yin and née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yue, Kuang, Qin 鈫 [?], Se 鏼, and Suo. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kuang Yue, registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an added-quota student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenbo; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kangyou; his grandfather was Zhixiong; his father was Cheng, and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Qi. He married a woman née He. He placed twelfth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Shao, registered in a military household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an added-quota student at the county school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dashao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangsheng; his grandfather, Duo, was a Station Master; his father, Qi, was an Instructor; and his mother was née Xie. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xuan and Feng 綘. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊恭〔貫武驤左衛官籍，順天府永清縣人，國子生，治詩經，字秉虔，行二，年三十七，六月初七日生〕。曾祖朗〔百戶〕，祖友〔百戶〕，父信，前母張氏，母周氏。永感下，兄玘，弟敬、泰，娶孫氏，繼娶郭氏、郭氏。順天府鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百五名。

劉諶〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字承芳，行三，年三十八，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖希先，祖惟脩，父源深，母周氏。慈侍下，兄訥，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第七十九名，會試第二百七十八名。
translation_en:
Gao Yuan 高垣, courtesy name Yongming, was registered in a military salt-producing household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangxin, his grandfather Ying, his father E, and his mother née Li; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Cheng, Bi, and Po, his younger brothers Shan, Pi, and Chi, and his wife was née Wang; he placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ji 陳璣, courtesy name Tianyi, was registered in a military officer household of Linqing Guard, Shandong, and was originally from Yuyao County, Zhejiang; a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Bin was a Company Commander, his grandfather Ding and father Xian were Deputy Battalion Commanders, and his mother was née Qiu; both parents were living, his younger brother was Yan, and he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently another woman née Zhang; he placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Gong 楊恭, courtesy name Bingqian, was registered in a military officer household of the Wuxiang Left Guard and was originally from Yongqing County, Shuntian Prefecture; a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lang and grandfather You were Company Commanders, his father was Xin, his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Zhou; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Qi, his younger brothers were Jing and Tai, and he married a woman née Sun, subsequently a woman née Guo, and then another woman née Guo; he placed thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chen 劉諶, courtesy name Chengfang, was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xixian, his grandfather Weixiu, his father Yuanshen, and his mother née Zhou; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Ne, and his wife was née Xiao; he placed seventy-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

仇惠〔貫直隸保定府安州新安縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字澤民，行五，年四十，六月初三日生。〕曾祖富，祖貴，父志〔訓導〕，母徐氏。永感下。兄恭、寬、信、敏，弟忠、恕。娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百五十名。

劉儒〔貫山東東昌府高唐州恩縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字寄道，行一，年三十二，十月十六日生。〕曾祖仲和，祖貴，父淮，前母陳氏，母賈氏。永感下。娶趙氏。山東鄉試第四十八名，會試第八十五名。

何淳〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣，軍籍，府學生，治易經，字宗厚，行一，年二十八，七月二十三日生。〕曾祖淮，祖榮〔遇例冠帶〕，父璋〔知州〕，母林氏。重慶下。兄沾〔同科進士〕，弟澡、冲、澋、派、溉、潞、淘、涴。娶李氏。廣東鄉試第十一名，會試第一百九十名。

熊紀〔貫河南南陽府南陽縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字時振，行四，年四十二，八月十一日生。〕曾祖普一，祖秀可，父琛，母張氏。永感下。兄懷、林、綱，弟理。娶王氏，繼娶李氏。河南鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百七十二名。
translation_en:
Qiu Hui, courtesy name Zemin, was registered in a civilian household in Xin’an County, Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged forty, born on the third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Zhi, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Gong, Kuan, Xin, and Min, and his younger brothers were Zhong and Shu. His wife was née Han. He placed seventy-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ru, courtesy name Jidao, was registered in a military household in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghe; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Huai. His father’s former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Jia. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Chun, courtesy name Zonghou, was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Huai; his grandfather, Rong, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under an applicable regulation; his father, Zhang, a Subprefect; and his mother, née Lin. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother Zhan was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year. His younger brothers were Zao, Chong, Jing, Pai, Gai, Lu, Tao, and Wan [?]. His wife was née Li. He placed eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Ji, courtesy name Shizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fourth in birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Puyi; his grandfather, Xiuke; his father, Chen; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huai, Lin, and Gang, and his younger brother was Li. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

王俸〔貫順天府通州三河縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字天爵，行一，年三十六，二月初七日生〕。曾祖敬〔知縣〕，祖祥〔贈員外郎〕，父文琮〔郎中〕，前母蔡氏、張氏，母宋氏。慈侍下，弟俊、僅、儒、倫，娶李氏，繼娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十一名，會試第二百九名。

translation_en:
Shu Sheng, registered in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Kongyang. Third in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wenxi, his grandfather Sheng, his father Chaojie, and his mother née Wu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Wang, and his younger brothers were Gao and Mian. He married a woman née Liang. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhu, registered in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and served as Instructor at the county school of Tongguan, Shaanxi. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxian. First in birth order, he was forty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Deyu; his grandfather Xuan was a Professor and received the honorary title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs. His father Shanji was Chief Supervising Secretary in that office, and his mother, née Feng, received the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ge, an honorary official for charitable service, Ji, Mo, Tan, Bang, Gui, Ke, and Gai. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Feng, registered in Sanhe County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Tianjue. First in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather Jing was a Magistrate; his grandfather Xiang was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director; and his father Wencong was a Director. His father's former wives were née Cai and née Zhang, and his mother was née Song. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Jun, Jin, Ru, and Lun. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He ranked 131st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xuan, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Dehui. Fourth in birth order, he was forty-four years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhiheng, his grandfather Shu, his father Xi, and his mother née Pan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Pao, a Prefectural Vice Prefect, Tang, and Shu; his younger brothers were Cheng, Chi, Yin, an honorary official for charitable service, Kai, Fang, Shou, and Long. He married a woman née Lu. He ranked 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

戴書〔貫湖廣武昌府崇陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字天錫，行二，年三十六，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖乾震，祖東津，父清〔知縣〕，前母曾氏，母金氏。慈侍下，兄聰，弟瑞，娶蒙氏。湖廣鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百六十四名。

黃宏〔貫南京京衛籍，浙江鄞縣人，應天府六合縣學生，治詩經，字德裕，行二，年三十三，六月十一日生〕。曾祖子良，祖福緣，父永慶，母張氏。具慶下，兄寶，娶林氏。應天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第一百十三名。
translation_en:
Pan Zhen, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, directly administered territory (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuqing. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Siwen, and his father Tan; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jue, Gong, and Guan, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked eighty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Hong, registered in Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongzhou. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyi, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Liang, an honorary official (yiguan); his mother was née Tang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Wei, and his younger brothers were Xiu and Tong. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He ranked one hundred twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Shu, registered in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tianxi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianzhen, his grandfather Dongjin, and his father Qing, a county magistrate. His father's former wife was née Zeng, and his mother was née Jin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Cong, his younger brother Rui, and his wife was née Meng. He ranked thirty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hong was registered with a capital guard in Nanjing and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a government school student in Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture, and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deyu. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Fuyuan, and his father Yongqing; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bao, and his wife was née Lin. He ranked one hundred tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

藍郁〔貫直隸淮安府塩城縣民籍，廣東茂名縣人，國子生，治詩經，字國馨，行一，年四十三，十月初八日生〕。曾祖文袍，祖盛，父春離，母蘇氏。永感下，弟都，娶汪氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十名，會試第六十二名。

吳祺〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣民籍，直隸灤州學學正，治詩經，字貴德，行八，年四十，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖子恒〔縣丞〕，祖繼能，父嗣正，母涂氏。具慶下，弟襃、裔，娶鄒氏，繼娶徐氏。江西鄉試第八十八名，會試第二百四十三名。

張諧〔貫福建福州府閩縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字汝諧，行九，年三十五，二月十一日生〕。曾祖聰〔知縣，贈主事〕，祖瑜〔貢士〕，父純〔知縣〕，母王氏。永感下，兄彬〔學正〕、模，弟經〔助教〕、相、槩〔貢士〕、柱，娶吳氏。福建鄉試第三名，會試第二百十五名。
translation_en:
He Hong, registered with the Standard-bearer Guard and a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuchou, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Shiyan, his father Qin, and his mother née Chen; his father was living and his mother deceased; his younger brothers were Jun, Yuan, and Qi, and his wife was née Su; he placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lan Yu, registered in a civilian household in Yancheng County, Huai’an Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Maoming County, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guoxin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenpao, his grandfather Sheng, his father Chunli, and his mother née Su; both parents were deceased; his younger brother was Du, and his wife was née Wang; he placed one hundred thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Qi, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Instructor at the Confucian school of Luanzhou, Zhili, specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guide, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ziheng, an Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Jineng, his father Sizheng, and his mother née Tu; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Bao and Yi, and he married a woman née Zou and subsequently a woman née Xu; he placed eighty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xie, registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruxie, he ranked ninth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cong, a Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his grandfather was Yu, a tribute scholar; his father was Chun, a Magistrate, and his mother was née Wang; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Bin, an Instructor, and Mo, and his younger brothers were Jing, an Assistant Instructor, Xiang, Gai, a tribute scholar, and Zhu; his wife was née Wu; he placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
An You, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Hao, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his father was Shangmin; his mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Qian. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhi, Zhen, and Zuo. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Xuan, courtesy name Gongzai, was registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, formerly a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Zongshan, Left Administrator; his father was Yingkui, a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Ping, and Jiao. He married a woman née Liang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Liang, courtesy name Wenming, was registered in Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, in an official household, and was a native of Dangtu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tai, a regular Chiliarch; his grandfather was Yuan; his father was Rui; and his mother was née Zheng. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kuan and Hong, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Liang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jian, courtesy name Kongzhao, was registered in Luanzhou Subprefecture, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Er; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Ju; and his mother was née Wang. Both his parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Kai and Zhen. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

何棐〔貫直隸揚州府泰興縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字輔之，行十七，年二十九，三月初四日生〕。曾祖濟〔旌表義民〕，祖顥，父岱〔兵馬指揮〕，母許氏，繼母陳氏。慈侍下，兄槩、樟〔應天府推官〕、林、槐、榆，弟棠〔貢士〕、桐、榛、栗，娶趙氏。應天府鄉試第二十一名，會試第十名。

孫沔〔貫山東兖州府魚臺縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字伯清，行三，年二十四，閏十月二十九日生〕。曾祖仲憲，祖瑛，父昶，前母王氏，母管氏。具慶下，兄漢、潮，娶陳氏。山東鄉試第六十一名，會試第一百四十六名。

陳霆〔貫浙江湖州府德清縣，匠籍，縣學生，治書經，字聲伯，行四，年二十七，十月初九日生〕。曾祖良，祖安，父和，母孫氏。具慶下，兄雲、雷、震，弟霽，娶胡氏。浙江鄉試第六名，會試第一百二十名。
translation_en:
Pan Xizeng, registered in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhonglu; he ranked fifth in the family and was twenty-seven sui, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Wenhua was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather Hong was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, additionally awarded the posthumous titles Grand Master for Governance and xiuzheng shuyin [?]; his father Zhang was Vice Surveillance Commissioner in charge of education. His mother, née Jiang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xiyu, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; Rong, an Assistant Instructor; and Xiyan. His younger brother was Zhi. He married a woman née Ye. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Fei, registered in Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Fuzhi; he ranked seventeenth in the family and was twenty-nine sui, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Ji was officially commended as a public-spirited commoner; his grandfather was Hao; and his father Dai was a Commander of a Wardens' Office. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Gai; Zhang, a Prefectural Judge of Yingtian Prefecture; Lin; Huai; and Yu. His younger brothers were Tang, a tribute scholar; Tong; Zhen; and Li. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Mian, registered in Yutai County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boqing; he ranked third in the family and was twenty-four sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian; his grandfather, Ying; and his father, Chang. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Guan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han and Chao. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ting, registered in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shengbo; he ranked fourth in the family and was twenty-seven sui, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, An; his father, He; and his mother, née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yun, Lei, and Zhen; his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

侯自明〔貫陝西西安府同州白水縣官籍，國子生，治詩經，字景德，行一，年三十，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖文禮，祖復〔教諭，贈右僉都御史〕，父恂〔右僉都御史〕，前母秦氏〔贈恭人〕，母劉氏〔封恭人〕。具慶下，弟自新、自勉〔官生〕、自同，娶井氏。陝西鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百八十二名。

凌雲翰〔貫應天府上元縣匠籍，國子生，治易經，字伯遠，行二，年四十一，八月十三日生〕。曾祖珍，祖子才〔贈南京戶部郎中〕，父文〔布政司左參議〕，前母趙氏〔贈宜人〕、李氏，母韓氏〔封宜人〕。永感下，兄雲翔，弟雲翱、雲翊、雲翀，娶王氏，繼娶邵氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第六十六名。

朱嘉會〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字亨之，行一，年二十三，五月初十日生〕。曾祖溥〔州同知〕，祖昱〔布政司司獄〕，父孔華〔監生〕，母鄭氏。重慶下，弟嘉祥、嘉賓、嘉議、嘉愛、嘉慶，娶衡氏。應天府鄉試第七十一名，會試第一百十一名。

陳寧〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字仕泰，行二，年三十一，七月初八日生〕。曾祖彭壽，祖正玄，父成聰，母潘氏。永感下，兄福，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第五十六名，會試第五十五名。
translation_en:
Hou Ziming, registered in an official household in Baishui County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingde, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenli; his grandfather, Fu, was a County School Instructor posthumously granted the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-chief; his father, Xun, was Right Assistant Censor-in-chief; his father’s former wife, née Qin, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Respect (gongren), and his mother, née Liu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Zixin, Zimian (a student admitted by virtue of his father’s official position), and Zitong; his wife was née Jing. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Yunhan, registered in an artisan household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Boyuan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Zicai, was posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father, Wen, was Left Administration Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father’s former wives were née Zhao, posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren), and née Li; his mother, née Han, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Yunxiang, and his younger brothers were Yun’ao, Yunyi, and Yunchong; he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shao. He ranked sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jiahui, registered in a civilian household in Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Hengzhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Pu, was a Subprefect; his grandfather, Yu, was a Prison Warden in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father, Konghua, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living; his younger brothers were Jiaxiang, Jiabin, Jiayi, Jia’ai, and Jiaqing; his wife was née Heng. He ranked seventy-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ning, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shitai, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pengshou; his grandfather was Zhengxuan; his father was Chengcong; his mother was née Pan. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Fu; his wife was née Huang. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Yi, courtesy name Deyu, was registered in a military household of the Weihui Battalion in Henan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Jing, and his father Liang; his father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Zhao. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother Jun was an honorary official, and his younger brother was Fu. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Zhai. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Shiqiao, courtesy name Minwang, was registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventh in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu, his grandfather Tong, and his father Shang, an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Su. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Yun, Xuan, and Shida, the last an honorary official; his younger brothers were Shi'ang and Shixian. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Ao, courtesy name Xizhao, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhizhong, his grandfather Huan, and his father Jiujing, a Registry Manager in a Guard; his mother and stepmother were both née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Fan. He married a woman née Wu. He placed forty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chun, courtesy name Yuanpu, was registered in a military household in Taihu County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youmin, his grandfather Defu, and his father Zhang, a Chief Geomancer; his mother was née Qin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rong and Lian. He married a woman née Ding. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Wo, registered in Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Cheng’en; he ranked fifteenth in family seniority, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the seventh day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Daochong, his grandfather Yongjing, and his father Zeng; his mother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuan, Jun, Ying, Mu, Li, and Shu, and his younger brother was Di. His wife was née Tong. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Duanming, registered in Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xidao; he ranked first in family seniority, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather Kui was a Registrar, and his father Fengyi was a Director of Studies. His father’s former wives were née Chen and née Mao; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Duanmian and Duanying, and his wife was née Xu. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qi, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongzhou; he ranked twenty-second in family seniority, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yizheng; his grandfather Ji was a Director of Studies; his father was Wu’an, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tai and Hua, and his younger brothers Meng, Zhen, and Dan. His wife was née Liu. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Hu, registered in Chongqing Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yixu; he ranked first in family seniority, was aged forty-six, and was born on the twelfth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin; his grandfather Yu was posthumously awarded the title of Subprefect; his father Bi was a Director of Studies, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi and Ji, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.
