translation_en:
Wu Chu 吳閦, courtesy name Tingjian, was registered in a civilian household in Taixing County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili); he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhen; his grandfather, Ying, had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his father was Zong, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Chan, and his younger brothers were Min, Wen, and Hong. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xian 張賢, courtesy name Shouyu, was registered in a civilian household in Sui Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian, his grandfather Chun, and his father Ning; his mother was née Lu, and his stepmother was née Wu. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Yun and Zan. His wife was née Li, and his subsequent wife was née Zhou. He placed seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Shaozheng 何紹正, courtesy name Jizong, was registered in a civilian household in Chun’an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xianwen; his grandfather, Tinglie, was granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his father, Li, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; and his mother, née Song, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Shaoming, and his younger brother was Shaoda. His wife was née Hong. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Zong 雷宗, courtesy name Xizeng, was registered in a military household of Longqing Left Guard in Zhili and was a native of Tongcheng County in Zhili; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Gao, his father Xin, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Xuan, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness. His wife was née Chen. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ou Yu 區玉 was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingzhang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenbi, his grandfather Dao, and his father Yu 愉; his mother was née Wei and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His wife was née Qu. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan 王鉉 was registered in a civilian household in Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong; the entry also associates him with Dingliao Left Guard in Liaodong [?]. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boju; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bocheng, his grandfather Hai, and his father Ning, a student of the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Xing and his stepmother née Bian. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Qi, an honorary official, and his younger brothers were Tang and Zheng. His wife was née Cai. He ranked eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Tai 俞泰 was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guochang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zonghai, his grandfather Sigong, and his father Qian; his mother was née Hou and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fu 復, Meng 蒙, Zhen 震, and Fu 孚. His wife was née Jin. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianxi 張天錫 was registered in a military household in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weifan; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuchu, his grandfather Xian, a commissioner, and his father Cui. His father's principal wife was née Peng, and his birth mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Tianyou, and his younger brothers were Tianfu, Tianlu, and Tianxu. His wife was née Jia. He ranked eighteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Yunzhen, courtesy name Tianyou, was registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the intercalary second month. His great-grandfather was Jiaxun; his grandfather, Xin; his father, Lian, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yunli, Yunlu, Yunyu, and Yunzhi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Zhong, courtesy name Lifu, was registered as a guardsman in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Xincheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shineng; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Shun; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was He, and his wife was née Jin. He placed 131st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Ye, courtesy name Ximeng, was registered in Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. An additional student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Sheng, a District Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Sizhong, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Xue, who had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhou, an honorary official; Lu and Han, both tribute scholars; and Jiao. His younger brother was Shi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Yue, courtesy name Yuanbo, was registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zonghao; his grandfather, Shi; and his father, Yi. His legal mother was née Fei, his stepmother née Wang, and his birth mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zuo, Li, and Hui; his younger brothers were Jin, Feng, Ting, Shen, Cai, and Dan. His wife was née Wu. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Ying, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunzhong. Fifteenth in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shantong; his grandfather was Meng (the annotation reads “buried” [?]); and his father was Liang. His legal mother was née Zhao, and his birth mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Ming (an honorary official); his younger brothers were Jun (an honorary official), Jie, Ren, Hua, and Qiao. He married a woman née Gui and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jie, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Hengfu. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-six and was born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaozong; his grandfather was Yuan (a county Confucian school Instructor, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue); and his father was Kai (Director in the Ministry of Revenue). His mother, née Xu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, née Gong, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Jian (Household Administrator of the Heir Apparent, concurrently an Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites). His younger brothers were Quan (a tribute scholar), Ce, Chi, and Fan. He married a woman née Xu. He ranked nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chunfang, registered in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shiyuan. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jia; his grandfather was Kongyong; his father was Dashou; and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chunbai, Chunchang, Chunfan, Chunkui, Chunshi, and Chunyan. He married a woman née Su. He ranked fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shen was registered in a military household of the Xi’an Rear Guard in Shaanxi and was a native of Pingliang County. He was an additional student at the Sanyuan County Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daofu. Eighth in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Ying (an honorary official); his father was Ming (a student of the Imperial University); and his mother was née Xue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ren, Zuo, Ru, Lun, Chuan, Xin, and Jun; his younger brothers were Jie, Wei, Jie, and Xie. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳璧〔貫山西太原府太谷縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字德如，行一，年三十九，八月初五日生〕。曾祖本，祖公海，父通，母田氏，繼母梁氏。具慶下，弟瑩，娶楊氏，繼娶趙氏。山西鄉試第十五名，會試第二百六十名。

于聰〔貫江西饒州府安仁縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字士達，行十九，年三十六，十二月初二日生〕。曾祖澄，祖禎，父甫，母何氏。重慶下，弟聘，娶何氏。江西鄉試第二十六名，會試第一百八十八名。
translation_en:
Zhang Zheng, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yidao, and he ranked fortieth in family order. He was twenty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Banghe; his grandfather, Shenfu, received the honorary title of Left Case Reviewer in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review; his father was Mao, and his mother was née Fang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Kuo, Jie, Gong, Bin, and Ze. His wife was née Yan. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Xin, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, and he ranked fourth in family order. He was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruxian, his grandfather Lian, and his father Shan; his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chuan, and his younger brothers were Zhong, Mian, and Xie. His wife was née Chen. He placed twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Bi, registered in Taigu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deru, and he ranked first in family order. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ben, his grandfather Gonghai, and his father Tong; his mother was née Tian, and his stepmother née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ying. His wife was née Yang, and his subsequent wife was née Zhao. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Cong, registered in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shida, and he ranked nineteenth in family order. He was thirty-six years old, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Fu; his mother was née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Pin, and his wife was née He. He placed twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
萬英〔貫順天府順義縣民籍，福建邵武縣人，國子生，治詩經，字子俊，行一，年三十八，四月二十七日生〕。曾祖光祖〔衞經歷〕，祖諒，父洪，前母蕭氏，母王氏，繼母劉氏。具慶下，弟宣、芳，娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第一百九十一名。

許瀚〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字彥卿，行三，年三十八，五月初六日生〕。曾祖子義，祖永斌，父評〔訓導〕，嫡母林氏，生母陳氏。永感下，兄仁〔左長史〕、彥充、彥器，娶陳氏，繼娶郭氏。福建鄉試第五十六名，會試第六十八名。

徐珙〔貫浙江金華府東陽縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字庭實，行十五，年三十一，二月十五日生〕。曾祖遠，祖鳳，父志，母任氏，繼母陳氏。慈侍下，兄璩、珂，弟瓘、碧，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第六十三名，會試第二百十一名。

吾哻〔貫浙江衢州府開化縣民籍，順天府文安縣學教諭，治書經，字廷介，行十九，年四十二，十月初九日生〕。曾祖江，祖體〔將仕佐郎，前訓導〕，父尋〔教諭〕，母方氏。具慶下，兄翀，弟翕〔教諭〕、翩、翬，娶方氏。浙江鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百八十四名。
translation_en:
Wan Ying 萬英, courtesy name Zijun, was registered in a civilian household in Shunyi County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Shaowu County, Fujian; a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Guangzu, a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Liang, and his father was Hong; his father's former wife was née Xiao, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Liu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Xuan and Fang, and his wife was née Zhao; he placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Han 許瀚, courtesy name Yanqing, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ziyi, his grandfather Yongbin, and his father Ping, an Assistant Instructor; his father's principal wife was née Lin and his birth mother née Chen; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Ren, a Left Chief Administrator, Yanchong, and Yanqi, and he married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Guo; he placed fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gong 徐珙, courtesy name Tingshi, was registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang; a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifteenth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Feng, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Ren and his stepmother née Chen; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brothers were Qu and Ke, his younger brothers Guan and Bi, and his wife was née Wang; he placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Han 吾哻, courtesy name Tingjie, was registered in a civilian household in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; an Instructor at the county government school of Wen'an County, Shuntian Prefecture, specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked nineteenth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jiang, his grandfather Ti, an Assistant Gentleman for Attending to Affairs and former Assistant Instructor, and his father Xun, an Instructor; his mother was née Fang; both parents were living, his elder brother was Chong, his younger brothers were Xi, an Instructor, Pian, and Hui, and his wife was née Fang; he placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Xun, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Huizhi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanliang; his grandfather, Chongxin; and his father, Zhonglun, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations. His father’s former wives were Lady Zhu, Lady Xu, and Lady Yan; his mother was Lady Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao and Gao, and his wife was Lady Wei. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Dai, registered in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Xifu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingde; his grandfather, Mu, was an Administrator; his father, Fengxian, was also an Administrator; and his mother was Lady Chu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yue, his younger brother was Yan, and his wife was Lady Dai. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jie, registered in Lingling County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Guoxin; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanheng; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Ying; and his mother, Lady Lei. Both parents were living, and his wife was Lady Liu. He placed forty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chi Kui, registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunchen; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Xin, was a prefectural Records Examiner; his father, Gong, was a Subprefect; and his mother was Lady Hao. His father was deceased and his mother living; his wife was Lady Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡鎮〔貫江西瑞州府高安縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字斯靖，行一，年三十九，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖克忠，祖源會，父瑞，母陳氏。重慶下，兄欽，娶鄒氏。江西鄉試第七十一名，會試第七十二名。

田綬〔貫湖廣荆州府松滋縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字大章，行四，年三十六，三月二十日生〕。曾祖文忠，祖誠，父瓊〔府學教授〕，嫡母彭氏，繼母王氏，生母趙氏。慈侍下，兄經、綸〔訓導〕、緯，弟繪、緒、維、繼、紹，娶仲氏。湖廣鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百四十五名。

姚隆〔貫南京留守後衛軍籍，直隸嘉定縣人，國子生，治詩經，字原學，行三，年三十一，二月初三日生〕。曾祖文榮，祖敬，父海，母華氏，繼母范氏。具慶下，兄陞，弟陁、隣、際，娶周氏。應天府鄉試第十七名，會試第一百六十七名。

陳鼎〔貫直隸永平府遷安縣民籍，江西新淦縣人，國子生，治易經，字汝和，行一，年三十，正月二十七日生〕。曾祖子倫，祖詰，父瑛，母王氏。重慶下，弟鼐，娶楊氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十二名，會試第一百九十五名。
translation_en:
Hu Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Gao’an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Sijing; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kezhong, his grandfather Yuanhui, his father Rui, and his mother née Chen. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Qin, and his wife was née Zou. He placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Shou, registered in a military household in Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dazhang; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhong, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Qiong, a Professor in a prefectural Confucian school. His legal mother was née Peng, his stepmother née Wang, and his birth mother née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun (an Assistant Instructor), and Wei; his younger brothers were Hui, Xu, Wei, Ji, and Shao. His wife was née Zhong. He placed thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Long, registered in a military household of the Nanjing Rear Guard of the Defending Garrison and originally from Jiading County in the directly administered region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanxue; he ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenrong, his grandfather Jing, his father Hai, his mother née Hua, and his stepmother née Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sheng; his younger brothers were Tuo, Lin, and Ji. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ding, registered in a civilian household in Qian’an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and originally from Xingan County, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruhe; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zilun, his grandfather Jie, his father Ying, and his mother née Wang. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Nai, and his wife was née Yang. He placed 132nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Kuizhao, registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenzhen, he ranked eleventh among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingyu, his grandfather Dejian, his father Sanyang, and his mother Lady Peng; his mother was living and his father deceased, his elder brothers were Wenya and Wendian, his younger brother was Wencui, and he married Lady Yang; he placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiamo, registered in a military household of the Ningxia Guard, Shaanxi, and originally from Laishui County in the Metropolitan Region, was a guard-school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shunqing, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Caifu, a department magistrate, his grandfather Shu, and his father Yi, a district magistrate; his father's principal wife was Lady Xu and his birth mother Lady Jin; both parents were living, he married Lady Geng, and he placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Mao, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wensu, he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, a bureau director in the Ministry of Works, his grandfather Dizhe, an assistant district magistrate, his father Kuan, a student of the Directorate of Education, and his mother Lady Qin; his mother was living and his father deceased, his elder brothers were Min and Dan, and he married Lady Ni; he placed ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Kuang, registered in an artisan household in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Cunyue, he ranked twenty-fifth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyong, his grandfather Zong, his father Pin, and his mother Lady Jiang; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Ye and Lie, his younger brother was Xuan, and he married Lady Ge; he placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yuanren 徐元稔, courtesy name Mingjia, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. He was Instructor at the county school of Shangrao, Jiangxi, and specialized in the Book of Documents. Eighth in family order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shifeng; his grandfather, Yuguang; his father, Keyu; and his mother, née Xiao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Yuancheng. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and held the partially illegible rank □四十三 [?] in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen You 陳猷, courtesy name Rujia, was registered in a military household in Yongchuan County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. Second in family order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengxi, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather, Ziheng; his father, Jin, a prefectural-school Instructor; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mo. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fiftieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qin 張芹, courtesy name Wenlin, was registered in a civilian household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. Fourth in family order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizhe; his grandfather, Hongben; his father, Jian, a County Magistrate; his mother, née Mao; and his stepmothers, née Chen and née Liao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiulin, and his younger brothers were Shanglin, Maolin, and Hualin. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ning Pu 甯溥, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in a medical household in Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. First in family order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhen; his grandfather, Ying, an Imperial Physician; his father, 𦚯 [reading uncertain]; and his mother, née Hou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Lian. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

葉相〔貫直隸揚州府江都縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字良臣，行二，年二十八，八月十四日生〕。曾祖坦〔國子監典籍〕，祖永年〔贈光祿寺署丞〕，父瀾〔光祿寺署正〕，前母趙氏〔贈孺人〕，母葛氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄槀，弟森、棐，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第八十九名，會試第五十四名。
translation_en:
Bian Chen 卞諶, courtesy name Xinqing, was from Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Ao; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shou, Xun, Yuan, Jian, E, and Hao, and his younger brothers Pu and Mo. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Biao 謝表, courtesy name Zhengbang, was from Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong, his grandfather Xian, and his father Yongzhen; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiong, Zhu, Bi, and Rui, and his younger brother Lian. His wife was née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yue 周鑰, courtesy name Xizhun, was from Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sanfu, his grandfather Ti, and his father Cheng, a county-school Instructor; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yue 鉞 and Zhen, and his younger brothers Zun and Ning. His wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Xiang 葉相, courtesy name Liangchen, was from Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Tan was Librarian in the Directorate of Education; his grandfather Yongnian was posthumously appointed Assistant Director of an office in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his father Lan was Director of an office in that court. His father's former wife, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his mother, née Ge, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Gao, and his younger brothers Sen and Fei. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiao Gao 蕭杲, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yanming, he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fuyi, his grandfather Yongcheng, his father Xuan, and his mother née Kong; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brothers were Xian and Zhi, and his wife was née Wang; he placed 129th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Liang 葉良, registered in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Hanjie, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghuan, his grandfather Zongren (granted the privilege of wearing official cap and sash under the applicable regulations), and his father Yueguang; his father's principal wife was née Xie, his stepmother née Zhou, and his birth mother née Chen; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brothers were Duan, Hang, Yu 迂, and Yu 遇, and his wife was née Chen; he placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yong 周用, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Xingzhi, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Xuan, his father Ang, and his mother née Ji; both parents were living, his younger brother was Tong, and his wife was née Shi; he placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Jie 薛价, registered in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Fanqing, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenmian, his grandfather Hong (a County Vice Magistrate), his father Jing (an Assistant Prefect), and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living, his elder brother was Kan, his younger brother Jixian (a consort of the imperial clan), and his wife was née Yang; he placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Yu 高嶼, courtesy name Zizhou, was registered with the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Quan, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Luan, a Translation Official, and Xiu, an Interpreter granted official cap and girdle; his younger brother was Cen. His wife was née Kang. He placed thirty-second in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xi 李錫, courtesy name Tianjue, belonged to a military household registered in Dong'an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Wenzhen; his father, Shi; and his mother, née Cao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jin and Yu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yi 陳義, courtesy name Yizhi, belonged to a civilian household registered in Raoping County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zong; his grandfather, Xicheng; his father, Guang; and his mother, née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Gang; his younger brothers were Zhiyong, Zhien, Zhiyuan, and Zhifang. His wife was née Zeng. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Xian 金賢, courtesy name Shixi, belonged to a civilian household registered in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather, Xunfu, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of State Ceremonial; his father, Yu; and his mother, née Ma. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Xiong, Ming, Xiu, and Lan, and his wife was née Ma. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

塗文祥〔貫江西南昌府靖安縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字舜徵，行十四，年二十七，正月初十日生〕。曾祖鳳韶〔封承德郎、工部主事〕，祖淮〔知府〕，父俽〔義官〕，母黃氏。重慶下，兄麒祥、儀祥，弟慶祥、獻祥，娶戴氏。江西鄉試第二十一名，會試第三十六名。

李深〔貫金吾右衛軍籍，順天府學附學生，治易經，字淵之，行一，年三十三，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖三公，祖英，父讓〔知縣〕，母孫氏。永感下，娶蘆氏。順天府鄉試第八十名，會試第二百五十二名。
translation_en:
Sun Wei 孫偉, courtesy name Chaowang, was registered in a civilian household in Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengfu; his grandfather, Ning, was a school instructor; his father was Rui, and his mother was née Li, both parents living; his younger brothers were Zuo (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Jie, and Fu, his wife was née Gong, and he placed ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Quan 屈銓, courtesy name Bingheng, was registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Hua Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Shen, his father Ning, and his mother née Sun, both parents living; his younger brothers were Yue, Qian, and Rui, his wife was née Shan, and he placed fortieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Wenxiang 塗文祥, courtesy name Shunzheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jing’an County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, ranked fourteenth in family order, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fengshao, had been honorarily invested as Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather, Huai, was a prefect; his father, Xin, held honorary official status for public benefaction, and his mother was née Huang; he had living grandparents and parents, his elder brothers were Qixiang and Yixiang, his younger brothers Qingxiang and Xianxiang, his wife was née Dai, and he placed twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shen 李深, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in a military household of the Jinwu Right Guard; he was an additional student at the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sangong, his grandfather Ying, his father Rang (a district magistrate), and his mother née Sun, both parents deceased; his wife was née Lu, and he placed eightieth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Ying 盧英, courtesy name Wenhua, was registered in a civilian household in Chongqing Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Yuanheng, his father Jigang, and his mother née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Hua, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Qin 姚欽, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in an artisan household under the Wugong Left Guard and was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sishan, his grandfather Zhong, his father Futong, and his mother née Pi. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Rui, Jin, and Zhen. His wife was née Chen; he subsequently married a woman née Han. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Lun 盧綸, courtesy name Chaoyan, was registered in a military household in Zengcheng County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiong, his grandfather Sui, his father Tingcan, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Xiao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jing and Kui, his younger brother was Gang, and his wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Wenbi 喻文璧, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Meizhou, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhang, his grandfather Jian, a Prefectural Judge, his father Yongzhong, a Station Master, and his mother née Peng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Wenyao and Wenhui, and his wife was née Deng. He placed fifty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Gun, registered with the Yongzhou Guard in Huguang and a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Qiong, and his father Yong, a tribute student (gongshi). His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Liu. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, a tribute student, and Bao; his younger brother was Biao. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Cong, of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Moufu; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zongyu, his grandfather Hui, his father Kongxu, and his mother née Yan. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Ming and Rui. He married a woman née Huang. He ranked third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county Confucian school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shifang; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Zhong was a Police Chief, posthumously granted the title of Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. His grandfather was Ji, his father Xu, a School Instructor, and his mother née Zeng. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Ming and Qin. He was betrothed to a woman née Hu. He ranked eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Feng, of Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianxiang; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shiduan, his grandfather Quan, his father Zong, and his mother née Zhai. His mother was still living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Luan; his younger brothers were Hong and Hu. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Kui 王奎, courtesy name Wenming, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Gongfu; and his mother, née Zang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yin and Kun. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Tang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Jingming 何景明, courtesy name Zhongmo, was registered in a civilian household in Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged seventeen, born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Jian, an Instructor in Yin-yang Studies; and his father, Xin, a Station Master. His father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jingshao, a District Magistrate; Jingyang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and Jinghui. He was betrothed to a woman née Zhang. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Zheng 顧正, courtesy name Shangcheng, was registered in a salt-producing household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yingquan; his grandfather, Ne, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under provisions of imperial favor; his father, Zhang; and his mother, née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ping and Zhong; his younger brothers were Zhi, Xian, Liang, Fang, Shan, and Neng. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yunpeng 張雲鵬, courtesy name Tianyi, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shan; his grandfather, Ning; his father, Hao, a Station Master; and his mother, née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qian, a Police Chief, and his younger brother was Yun'e. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-first in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Jike, registered in a military household in Gucheng County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongyu; he ranked tenth among his brothers and was aged twenty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianqing; his grandfather, Rong, was posthumously appointed a County Magistrate; his father, Zi, was an Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Wu, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhe and Xianke, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Fu. His wife was née Han. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yu, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yourong; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Zhihe, and his father Xuancong; his father's former wife was née Gong, and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Ru, and Zhao, the last an official awaiting selection for appointment; his younger brothers were Han, Lu, Jiang, and You. His wife was née Ming. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shu, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Congxue; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hong, was a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Qianfu; his father, Mixuan, was an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Hong, and his stepmother was née You. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kan, Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Yin. His wife was née Fang. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Zhong, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yafu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingyan, his grandfather Daobao, and his father Furun; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Shao. His parents and grandparents were all deceased. His elder brother was Jin. His wife was née Ou; he subsequently married a woman née Deng. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shi, registered in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiuqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shicong, his grandfather Yin, his father Zhao, and his mother Lady Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rong and Yin. He married Lady Zhu. He placed sixteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Xiang, registered in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yongxiu; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi, his grandfather □ [illegible], his father Jian, a Registrar, and his mother Lady Wu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were □ [illegible] and Qing [?]. He married Lady Ming and subsequently Lady Tian. He placed nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Zhan, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zongze; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuancheng, his grandfather Jinglong, his father Yu, and his mother Lady Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qian, Chun (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Tang, Yong, Shu, and Fa. He married Lady Cai and subsequently Lady Lu. He placed twelfth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shiwang, registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Fulin; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Rongzhuang, his grandfather Jiezhong, his father E, and his mother Lady Wang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhong, an Instructor, Tan, Shizhan, and Shibiao; his younger brother was Shike. He married Lady Xie. He placed eighty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張顒〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣，民籍，儒士，治易經，字子孚，行四，年三十三，四月初四日生〕。曾祖元寶，祖昭胖，父晟，母陳氏。永感下，弟穎，娶龔氏。福建鄉試第六十七名，會試第四十二名。

師燮〔貫陝西西安府長安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝和，行二，年二十六，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖榮，祖珎，父禮〔知縣〕，母田氏。具慶下，兄皐、夔，弟龍，娶田氏。陝西鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百八十三名。

曽大顯〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣，軍籍，府學增廣生，治禮記，字世榮，行四，年三十三，九月十七日生〕。曾祖思恭，祖應通，父啓〔教諭，贈知縣〕，嫡母楊氏〔贈孺人〕，生母楊氏〔封太孺人〕。慈侍下，兄賢〔學正〕、大賓、大有〔監察御史〕，娶李氏，繼娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第三名，會試第一百八十六名。
translation_en:
Liu An, courtesy name Yijing, was registered in Datong County, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenqing; his grandfather, Zheng, was posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel; and his father, Wen, was Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission. His father's former wife, née Xu, received the title Lady (yiren); his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Tianlu, formerly a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard, and Tianjue, an honorary official (yiguan); his younger brother was Ning. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yong, courtesy name Zifu, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanbao, his grandfather Zhaopang, his father Sheng, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Gong. He placed sixty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Xie, courtesy name Ruhe, was registered in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Zhen, his father Li, a District Magistrate, and his mother née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gao and Kui; his younger brother was Long. He married a woman née Tian. He placed thirty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Daxian, courtesy name Shirong, was registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A supplementary student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fourth in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong; his grandfather, Yingtong; and his father, Qi, a School Instructor posthumously appointed District Magistrate. His legal mother, née Yang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his birth mother, also née Yang, received the title Dowager Lady (tai ruren). His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Xian, a School Director; Dabin; and Dayou, an Investigating Censor. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

凃敬〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，民籍，儒士，治書經，字寅之，行八，年二十八，七月初九日生〕。曾祖自彰，祖彬文，父瑄〔教諭〕，母鄔氏。重慶下，兄蔓、芳，弟蕡、蘊、薇、蘅、萇、茂，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第二十三名，會試第二百五十八名。
translation_en:
Zhang Lian 張璉, courtesy name Ruqi, was from Yaozhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congzheng; his grandfather, Qing, was granted the title of Prefectural Judge; his father, Jun, was a Prefectural Judge; and his mother, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Heng, Shu, and Zhen, and his wife was née Ren. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Le 符樂, courtesy name Tonghe, was from Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was forty-two sui, born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youmao; his grandfather was Tang; his father, Xin, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Zou. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhen, Yu, Zhuo, and Xi, and his wife was née Xiao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Kan 郁侃, courtesy name Xizheng, was from Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-five sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather was Meng; his father was Qiong; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Lun, Ru, and Qiao. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Dong. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Jing 凃敬, courtesy name Yinzhi, was from Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was twenty-eight sui, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhang; his grandfather was Binwen; his father, Xuan, was an Instructor; and his mother was née Wu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Man and Fang; his younger brothers were Fen, Yun, Wei, Heng, Chang, and Mao. His wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Duo 李鐸, courtesy name Kongjiao, was registered in a military household in Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather was Kai; his father was Min, County Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu, Tang (a tribute scholar), Feng (a medical official), Xi, and Qin. His wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Zhao 沈炤, courtesy name Wenming, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Chi, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations; his grandfather was Fu, officially honored for filial piety; his father was Liang; and his mother was née Gong. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yao, Zhuo (a tribute scholar), Xi, Xun, Xu, Yue, Xiu, Lie, Wei, and Tao. His wife was née Yan. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yurong 吳玉榮, courtesy name Guiqing, was registered in a military household of Taiyuan Left Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Qianshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yongxu; his grandfather was Xiyuan; his father was Ziyu; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuyong, and his wife was née Yao. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Luan 王鑾, courtesy name Gongzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangcheng County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a Subprefect of the Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather was Sheng, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father was Xiang, Director in the Ministry of Revenue, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Court Service (chaolie dafu); and his mother was née Sheng, invested with the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jin, Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and his wife was née Xu. He placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Fu, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouren; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qianfu; his grandfather was Mixuan, an Assistant Instructor [?]; and his father was Yin. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Fang. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian and Wen, and he married a woman of the Zhang family. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ang, registered in a military household in Gaoling County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of an illegible category [?], specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingju; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old; his birth date is illegible. His great-grandfather was Liu; his grandfather was Liang; and his father was Lu, a Police Chief [?]. His mother was née Ma, followed by an illegible annotation concerning a family name [?]. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sheng; an annotation records marriage to a woman of the Wu family [?]. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 1□□th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yangchun, registered in a civilian household in Qu County, Guang'an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zongyuan; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Chaofu; his grandfather was Yunzhong; and his father was Fang, a District Magistrate [?]. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Renchun, Yuchun, Jiechun, Zhichun, Xinchun, and Yanchun, and he married a woman of the Wu family. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jing, registered in a military household of Dali Guard, Yunnan, and a native of Changshu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zaidao; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Dayong; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Cheng; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gang and Ji, and he married a woman of the Jiang family. He placed forty-first in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕膺
天命承
祖宗
列聖之統以臨天下
于兹十有五年夙
===
夜兢兢思弘化理
非法諸古而不可
然嘗考之前代繼
統之君守成稱賢
莫盛於夏之啓商

===

translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: “I have received Heaven’s mandate and inherited the succession of my ancestors, the sage sovereigns, to rule All under Heaven. It has now been fifteen years. Vigilant day and night, I have sought to extend moral transformation and good government; this cannot be achieved without taking antiquity as a model. Yet when I have examined the rulers of former dynasties who inherited the succession and were praised as worthy for preserving their predecessors’ achievements, none surpassed Qi of Xia and those of Shang…

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
之中宗高宗周之
成康之數君者治
績之美具在方策
果何道以致之近
世儒者之論謂聖
===
王以求任輔相為
先又謂君之聖者
以辨君子與小人
數君之致治也其
亦有待於是邪且

translation_en: …Zhongzong and Gaozong of Shang, and Cheng and Kang of Zhou: the splendid achievements of these rulers in governing are all recorded in written accounts. By what means, indeed, did they accomplish this? Recent Confucian scholars have argued that sage kings give priority to seeking out and appointing chief ministers, and that a ruler’s sageliness lies in distinguishing gentlemen from petty men. Did these rulers’ attainment of good government likewise depend upon this? Furthermore…

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
輔相之賢否君子
小人之情狀未易
知也茲欲簡賢為
輔用君子不惑於
小人將安所據邪
===
天下之務固非一
端以今日之所急
者言之若禮樂若
教化若選才課績
征賦之法兵刑之

punctuated:
輔相之賢否、君子小人之情狀，未易知也。茲欲簡賢為輔，用君子，不惑於小人，將安所據邪？

天下之務，固非一端。以今日之所急者言之，若禮樂，若教化，若選才課績、征賦之法、兵刑之
translation_en:
…whether chief ministers are worthy or unworthy, and the dispositions and conduct of gentlemen and petty men, are not easily known. Now, wishing to select worthy men as chief ministers, employ gentlemen, and avoid being misled by petty men, what should We rely upon?

The affairs of the realm are certainly manifold. To speak of the pressing concerns of today: rites and music, moral instruction, methods for selecting talent, evaluating performance, and levying taxes, and those pertaining to military affairs and punishments…

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
令皆斟酌于古然
行之既久不能無
弊焉祛其弊而救
之欲化行政舉如
祖宗創制之初比隆
===
前代何施何為而
得其道邪子諸生
績學明經通於古
今之宜其具實以
對毋隱言毋泛論

行之既久不能無

之欲化行政舉如
祖宗創制之初比隆
===
前代何施何為而
得其道邪予諸生
績學明經通於古
今之宜其具實以
對毋隱言毋泛論
punctuated: 令，皆斟酌于古，然行之既久，不能無弊焉。祛其弊而救之，欲化行政舉，如祖宗創制之初，比隆前代，何施何為而得其道邪？子諸生績學明經，通於古今之宜，其具實以對，毋隱言，毋泛論。
translation_en: …regulations—all have been framed with due consideration of antiquity. Yet, having been implemented for so long, they cannot be free of defects. To remove these defects and remedy them, so that moral transformation may take effect and government may function as when Our ancestors first established the institutions, matching the flourishing rule of former dynasties—what measures and actions would achieve the proper way? You students have accumulated learning and elucidated the Classics, and understand what is appropriate to past and present. Set out the facts fully in your replies; withhold nothing and avoid generalities.

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
臣康海
臣對臣聞天下有不可易之道而常獲於人
主有不敢易之心蓋天下之事未有舍道而
能集者而道固不可易也心之所向道之弘
否所關一有所易則所以脩乎身者必不能
實用其力而道之在我知之不明守之不固
甫遷於此或轉於彼雖欲勤勵以求治而弛
張予奪一無所據窺伺媒孽之輩共起而乘
之雖有賢人君子立於其朝漫不相信甚者
或斥譴罷去不為之所天下之治將焉所賴
===
而成乎惟有以真知道之不可易其心常憂
勤惕厲而不敢以一毫苟且輕率之意雜之
於中擇之必精執之必固使用人取善各有
定則賢否莫吾亂而君子小人不相尤既得
其人而任之以事則政無不舉而法無不振
天下之治宜無有不成者矣古之人君未有
不達於是而能致其治者也亦未有徒達於
是其心終有易焉而能以無弊者也洪惟
皇帝陛下以至聖之德撫盈成之運十五年来民
安物阜雖堯舜禹湯文武之業亦不過此而

臣康海

臣對：臣聞天下有不可易之道，而常獲於人主有不敢易之心。蓋天下之事，未有舍道而能集者，而道固不可易也。心之所向，道之弘否所關。一有所易，則所以脩乎身者必不能實用其力，而道之在我，知之不明，守之不固。甫遷於此，或轉於彼，雖欲勤勵以求治，而弛張予奪，一無所據。窺伺媒孽之輩，共起而乘之。雖有賢人君子立於其朝，漫不相信，甚者或斥譴罷去，不為之所。天下之治，將焉所賴而成乎？惟有以真知道之不可易，其心常憂勤惕厲，而不敢以一毫苟且輕率之意雜之於中，擇之必精，執之必固，使用人取善各有定則，賢否莫吾亂，而君子小人不相尤。既得其人，而任之以事，則政無不舉，而法無不振，天下之治宜無有不成者矣。古之人君，未有不達於是而能致其治者也；亦未有徒達於是，其心終有易焉，而能以無弊者也。

洪惟皇帝陛下，以至聖之德，撫盈成之運。十五年来，民安物阜，雖堯舜禹湯文武之業，亦不過此，而
translation_en:
Your servant, Kang Hai.

Your servant replies: I have heard that there is an unalterable Way governing all under Heaven, and that its constant realization depends upon the ruler possessing a heart that dares not change [?]. For no undertaking under Heaven has ever succeeded by abandoning the Way; the Way assuredly cannot be altered. Whether the Way flourishes depends upon the direction of the heart. Once that direction changes, one necessarily fails to exert genuine effort in cultivating oneself; one’s understanding of the Way is unclear, and one’s adherence to it insecure. No sooner has one shifted here than one turns elsewhere. Even if one wishes to strive diligently for good government, one has no grounds for deciding when to relax or tighten measures, grant or take away. Those who watch for opportunities and foment trouble rise together to exploit this. Even when worthy and principled men stand at the ruler’s court, he gives them no trust; worse still, he may denounce, reprimand, and dismiss them, leaving them no place [?]. Upon what, then, can good government throughout the realm depend for its achievement?

Only by truly recognizing that the Way cannot be altered, keeping one’s heart ever concerned, diligent, watchful, and resolute, and daring not admit the slightest trace of expediency or rashness, can one choose with discrimination and hold fast with firmness. Then there will be fixed standards both for employing men and for adopting what is good; neither the worthy nor the unworthy will confuse one’s judgment, and gentlemen and petty men will not reproach one another. Once the right men have been found and entrusted with affairs, every measure of government will be carried out and every law given effect. Good government throughout the realm should then assuredly be achieved. Among the rulers of antiquity, none ever achieved good government without understanding this. Nor did any merely understand it, yet ultimately change his heart, and still remain free of failings.

I reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed with the virtue of supreme sagehood, presides over an age of full accomplishment. For fifteen years the people have enjoyed peace and goods have been abundant. Even the achievements of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu did not surpass this, yet…

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
策士之詔乃猶惓惓焉以化之不弘治之不洽
為念
陛下豈誠有未達於是而猶待於問哉臣有以仰
窺
聖心之於道固有不自易焉者也臣嘗謂古今豪
傑之士不得所遇雖子思孟軻之流亦且徒
爾而臣之庸昧乃際遇若此臣敢有所諱而
不言哉臣惟天下之深患在於久安極治而
機括所不見者莫為之虞
陛下夙夜兢兢思弘化理此固宜也然用於己不
===
若資於人求諸今莫若法乎古古之君心純
乎道未嘗敢以為易故其用人行政有非後
世之所能及如啓當禪授之後繼禹之業守
之以敬而伯益之用終始無間故道之得於
禹者無廢墜不舉者矣中宗高宗一切信任
陟扈傅說之屬而又本以嚴恭寅畏恭默思
道之心成商之治夫豈無所據邪殷之頑民
雜於管蔡武庚之手武王之澤未洽也使非
悔悟於周公篤信於君奭偕有成康繼序不
忘之思旌別淑慝之意而禮樂之化豈能如

punctuated: 策士之詔，乃猶惓惓焉，以化之不弘、治之不洽為念。陛下豈誠有未達於是，而猶待於問哉？臣有以仰窺聖心之於道，固有不自易焉者也。臣嘗謂古今豪傑之士，不得所遇，雖子思、孟軻之流，亦且徒爾。而臣之庸昧，乃際遇若此，臣敢有所諱而不言哉？臣惟天下之深患，在於久安極治，而機括所不見者，莫為之虞。陛下夙夜兢兢，思弘化理，此固宜也。然用於己，不若資於人；求諸今，莫若法乎古。古之君，心純乎道，未嘗敢以為易，故其用人行政，有非後世之所能及。如啓當禪授之後，繼禹之業，守之以敬，而伯益之用，終始無間，故道之得於禹者，無廢墜不舉者矣。中宗、高宗，一切信任陟扈、傅說之屬，而又本以嚴恭寅畏、恭默思道之心，成商之治，夫豈無所據邪？殷之頑民，雜於管蔡、武庚之手，武王之澤未洽也。使非悔悟於周公，篤信於君奭，偕有成康繼序不忘之思、旌別淑慝之意，而禮樂之化，豈能如
translation_en:
…yet in the edict calling upon scholars to answer policy questions, you remain earnestly concerned that moral transformation has not spread widely and good government has not reached everywhere. Can Your Majesty truly have failed to comprehend this and still need to ask? Your servant can thereby perceive something of your sagely mind: in its approach to the Way, it assuredly never permits itself to take matters lightly.

Your servant has often reflected that outstanding men, past and present, who fail to find their opportunity—even men such as Zisi and Meng Ke—can accomplish nothing. Yet someone as mediocre and ignorant as your servant has encountered an opportunity such as this. Would I dare conceal anything and leave it unsaid? I believe that the gravest danger to the realm lies in prolonged peace and consummate order, when no one takes precautions against developments whose workings remain unseen. Your Majesty is vigilant morning and night, intent upon extending moral transformation and good government. This is certainly fitting. Yet relying on your own efforts is less effective than drawing upon others; seeking guidance in the present is less effective than taking antiquity as your model.

The rulers of antiquity devoted their minds wholly to the Way and never dared regard it as easy. Thus, in employing men and conducting government, they achieved things beyond the reach of later ages. For example, Qi came after the age of succession by abdication, inherited Yu’s enterprise, and preserved it with reverence. His employment of Bo Yi remained uninterrupted from beginning to end; thus nothing of the Way received from Yu was allowed to lapse or remain unpracticed. Zhongzong and Gaozong placed complete trust in men such as Zhi Hu [?] and Fu Yue. Moreover, they grounded their rule in minds marked by solemn reverence and awe, respectful silence and reflection upon the Way, thereby bringing about the good government of Shang. Surely their achievements had a foundation?

The recalcitrant people of Yin were entangled with Guan, Cai, and Wu Geng, for King Wu’s beneficence had not yet reached them fully. Had there been no remorse and awakening concerning the Duke of Zhou, no firm trust in Lord Shi, and, together with these, no resolve such as Cheng and Kang possessed to continue the succession without forgetting their predecessors, nor any intention to distinguish the good from the wicked, how could the transforming influence of rites and music have been as…

title: 弘治十五年進士登科錄
text:
詩書所道哉程頤曰聖王以求任輔相為先
歐陽脩曰君之聖者以辨君子與小人盖政
以人而舉人既存則政自無偏弊不舉之患
而治之在天下者可成也
陛下欲求數君致治之績獨可舍此而他務邪亦
惟有不敢易之心而已天下之政孰有出於
人主之心者况用人之際又其本原所自之
地哉
聖制所謂簡賢為輔用君子不惑於小人誠灼見
其必然而憂勤之心有不能自已者也盖大
===
===
君為天地之宗子必有大臣以為宗子之家
相相之職所以輔養君德而贊成政化天子
不可一日無者豈惟夏商周為然皐夔稷契
之流雖堯舜之世亦不可無也若其賢與否
則必辨之於先而後可任之於後苟辨之不
明用之不當則天下之禍反有不可言者矣
何者以匹夫之賤而上與天子共事其所為
操縱予奪者無一不為天下之所稟受使心
術或不正而學識或不醇則其所壞非如有
司之一節一端而已故必先有不敢易之心
